paper_title: Prior and Posterior Networks: A Survey on Evidential Deep Learning Methods For Uncertainty Estimation
paper_abstract: Popular approaches for quantifying predictive uncertainty in deep neural networks often involve multiple sets of weights or models, for instance, via ensembling or Monte Carlo dropout. These techniques usually incur overhead by having to train multiple model instances or do not produce very diverse predictions. This survey aims to familiarize the reader with an alternative class of models based on the concept of Evidential Deep Learning: For unfamiliar data, they admit “what they don’t know” and fall back onto a prior belief. Furthermore, they allow uncertainty estimation in a single model and forward pass by parameterizing distributions over distributions. This survey recapitulates existing works, focusing on the implementation in a classification setting, before surveying the application of the same paradigm to regression. We also reflect on the strengths and weaknesses compared to each other as well as to more established methods and provide the most central theoretical results using a unified notation in order to aid future research.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
This survey paper looks at Evidential Deep Learning methods, mentioning and relating many different papers, as summarised in Figure 1 and Tables 1, 2 and 3. This includes methods for classification and regression, as well as prior-based and posterior-based methods.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
Strengths 1. The paper covers many different papers / methods. 2. Sections 1, 2, 3.1 and 3.2 are well-written, and easy to follow. I also thought the Discussion brought up some nice points. Weaknesses 1. I found the explanations of the methods very brief and terse in Sections 3.3, 3.4 and 4. There was typically a couple of sentences assigned to each paper, and I was not able to follow how each method was different. This starts at the top of page 7. It seems like the authors assume that the reader is familiar with the papers, and this is just a brief summary of the methods like what would be in a space-pressured 'Related Works' section in a paper. As someone who does not know most of the recent works discussed in this survey paper, I was unable to follow most of the explanations. 2. The authors claim they compare Evidential Deep Learning approaches to established methods (as said at the top of page 2). Where was this done? Was this Section 5, and if so, I did not find this to be much of a discussion (it is just a few quick sentences on other approaches without much insight). 3. The authors say they provide the "most central theoretical results using a unified notation" (Abstract). This was not clear to me in the main paper at all. Most methods are mentioned but I am unsure what the most central results are and where in the paper they are. Most of the equations appear in the background section, and I believe most surveyed papers would already describe Dirichlet distributions. 4. The discussion on Model uncertainty in Section 3.2 was a bit weird to me. The authors previously argued that we lost epistemic uncertainty by using a single estimate of neural network weights, but now say that the uncertainty is still available. I think the authors should change some of the writing around Equation 4 so this does not seem so out-of-place / contradictory. 5. Figure 2 is not explained in much detail. I was often confused as to how each of the subplots in Figure 2 represents what the authors say it represents, and nowhere is this explained to the reader (instead, the authors just assume knowledge of eg how Fig 2d represents model uncertainty while 2c represents data uncertainty). Ideally, in my opinion, the authors should have a detailed caption (or detail in Section 2) explaining each of the subplots and comparing them to each other.

**Requested Changes:**
Many of my requested changes are detailed in the Weaknesses section above. 1. My biggest problem with the paper was my inability to follow the brief explanations of methods from Section 3.3 onwards. As a survey paper, I think the authors should have better writing so that I can follow each method and understand the big picture view of how they differ from each other. [See Weakness 1] 2. The authors claim they compare approaches to established methods, and also critically reflect on their advantages and shortcomings. Similar to point 1 above, I did not think this was done in a readable way or in sufficient detail. [Also see weakness 2] 3. [See Weakness 3] I did not follow what the most central theoretical results are. Could the authors make this more obvious and/or argue to me why this is a useful contribution. (Note that I have not read most of the surveyed papers, so am willing to be convinced that they are unaware of each other or use significantly different notation. But if this is the case, then perhaps the authors should make this clearer in the writing.) 4. See Weakness 4 and suggested change. 5. See Weakness 5 and suggested change. 6. I thought the Discussion brought up some valid problems with methods, but again, this was mentioned briefly and only at the end of the paper. Could some of these ideas be put in during the rest of the paper and in significantly more detail, so the methods are critically discussed throughout? Minor typos: (a) 'i.e.' should be 'e.g.' bottom of page 2. (b) "probability *of* success" (bottom of page 2). (c) "a more complex teacher network" [no 's'] (top of page 7). (d) Greek letter 'nu' instead of 'v' in $\mathcal{N}(\gamma, \sigma^2 v^{-1})$ bottom of page 9? (e) "quanitified" -> "quantified" top of page 10.

**Broader Impact Concerns:**
No Broader Impact Statement provided, and I do not think one is required.

**Rebuttal Comments:**
Reponse to Reviewer 6GHq: We would like to thank the anonymous reviewer for their tremendously useful feedback to our work. We corrected the caught typos and implemented a lot of the suggestions to further improve the paper. We address a few more of the raised points here: - Based on the feedback of the other reviewers, we welcome the idea of further discussing the showcased approaches in sections 3 and 4, which so far happened in an abridged version to stay within the 12 page limit. - We changed the wording of comparing EDL approaches to established methods in order not to imply new empirical results, which might have been misleading. The comparison indeed takes place within the discussion, and we will take this point along with the concerns of reviewer jdKi to extend the discussion of this point in the main text. - Addressing weakness 4 as well as a point raised by reviewer jdKi, we will add an additional section discussion the ways epistemic uncertainty are obtained within the EDL framework and how this compares to other UQ approaches such as ensembling.
paper_title_zh: 先验与后验网络：证据深度学习方法在不确定性估计中的综述
paper_abstract_zh: 流行的方法在量化深度神经网络中的预测不确定性时，通常涉及多组权重或模型，例如通过集成或蒙特卡洛dropout。这些技术通常需要训练多个模型实例而产生额外开销，或者无法产生非常多样化的预测。本综述旨在使读者熟悉基于证据深度学习概念的另一类模型：对于不熟悉的数据，它们承认“它们不知道的”，并回退到先验信念。此外，它们通过参数化分布之上的分布，允许在单个模型和前向传播中进行不确定性估计。本综述回顾了现有工作，重点关注分类设置中的实现，然后调查同一范式在回归中的应用。我们还反思了彼此之间以及与更成熟方法的优缺点，并使用统一的符号提供了最核心的理论结果，以助力未来的研究。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
这篇综述论文探讨了证据深度学习方法，提及并关联了许多不同的论文，如图1和表1、2、3所示。这包括分类和回归方法，以及基于先验和后验的方法。

**优点与不足：**
优点：
1. 论文涵盖了许多不同的论文/方法。
2. 第1、2、3.1和3.2节写得很好，易于理解。我也认为讨论部分提出了一些很好的观点。

不足：
1. 我发现第3.3、3.4和4节对方法的解释非常简略和晦涩。通常每篇论文只有几句话的描述，我无法理解每种方法的不同之处。这种情况从第7页顶部开始。作者似乎假定读者熟悉这些论文，而这只是一个类似论文中“相关工作”部分因篇幅限制而简略的方法总结。作为一个对这篇综述论文中讨论的大部分近期工作不甚了解的人，我无法理解大部分的解释。
2. 作者声称他们比较了证据深度学习方法与已建立的方法（如第2页顶部所述）。这在何处进行了？是在第5节吗？如果是，我没有发现这里有太多的讨论（只是对其他方法进行了几句简短的描述，没有太多洞见）。
3. 作者说他们提供了“使用统一符号的最核心的理论结果”（摘要）。我在正文中完全不清楚这一点。大多数方法都被提及，但我不确定最核心的结果是什么，以及它们在论文的哪个部分。大多数方程出现在背景部分，我相信大多数被调查的论文已经描述了狄利克雷分布。
4. 第3.2节关于模型不确定性的讨论在我看来有些奇怪。作者之前认为通过使用单一神经网络权重的估计，我们失去了认识不确定性，但现在又说这种不确定性仍然存在。我认为作者应该在方程4周围的文字做一些修改，以免显得如此不合时宜/矛盾。
5. 图2没有详细解释。我经常困惑于图2中的每个子图如何代表作者所说的内容，而且文中没有对此进行解释（相反，作者只是假定读者知道例如图2d代表模型不确定性而2c代表数据不确定性）。在我看来，理想情况下，作者应该有一个详细的图注（或在第2节中详细说明），解释每个子图并将它们相互比较。

**请求的修改：**
我请求的许多修改已在上述不足部分详细说明。
1. 我对这篇论文最大的问题是，从第3.3节开始，我无法理解对方法的简略解释。作为一篇综述论文，我认为作者应该有更好的写作，以便我能理解每种方法并了解它们之间差异的全貌。[参见不足1]
2. 作者声称他们比较了方法与已建立的方法，并对其优缺点进行了批判性反思。与上述第1点类似，我认为这一点没有以可读的方式或足够的细节进行。[也参见不足2]
3. [参见不足3] 我不清楚最核心的理论结果是什么。作者能否使其更明显，并/或向我论证为什么这是一个有用的贡献。（请注意，我没有阅读大部分被调查的论文，所以愿意被说服它们彼此不了解或使用显著不同的符号。但如果是这样，那么作者或许应该在写作中更清楚地说明这一点。）
4. 参见不足4和建议的修改。
5. 参见不足5和建议的修改。
6. 我认为讨论部分提出了一些方法的有效问题，但同样，这只是简略提及并在论文末尾。能否将其中一些观点在论文其余部分以更详细的篇幅提出，以便对方法进行批判性讨论？

小错误：
(a) 第2页底部的“i.e.”应为“e.g.”。
(b) 第2页底部的“probability *of* success”。
(c) 第7页顶部的“a more complex teacher network” [无需's']。
(d) 第9页底部的$\mathcal{N}(\gamma, \sigma^2 v^{-1})$中的希腊字母'nu'是否应为'v'？
(e) 第10页顶部的“quanitified” -> “quantified”。

**更广泛影响关注：**
未提供更广泛影响声明，我认为也不需要。

**反驳意见：**
对评审员6GHq的回应：我们感谢匿名评审员对我们工作的极其有用的反馈。我们纠正了发现的错误，并实施了许多建议以进一步改进论文。我们在此再回应一些提出的观点：
- 基于其他评审员的反馈，我们欢迎在3和4节进一步讨论所展示的方法，这在之前因限于12页篇幅而进行了简略处理。
- 我们修改了将EDL方法与已建立方法进行比较的措辞，以免误导读者认为有新的实证结果。比较确实在讨论中进行，我们将结合评审员jdKi的关注点，在正文中扩展这一点的讨论。
- 针对不足4以及评审员jdKi提出的一个观点，我们将增加一个额外部分，讨论在EDL框架内如何获得认识不确定性，以及这与集成等其他UQ方法的比较。

paper_title: Discipline-specific open access publishing practices and barriers to change: an evidence-based review
paper_abstract:
Background: Many of the discussions surrounding Open Access (OA) revolve around how it affects publishing practices across different academic disciplines. It was a long-held view that it would be only a matter of time before all disciplines fully and relatively homogeneously implemented OA. Recent large-scale bibliometric studies show, however, that the uptake of OA differs substantially across disciplines. We aimed to answer two questions: First, how do different disciplines adopt and shape OA publishing practices? Second, what discipline-specific barriers to and potentials for OA can be identified? 
 Methods: In a first step, we identified and synthesized relevant bibliometric studies that assessed OA prevalence and publishing patterns across disciplines. In a second step, and adopting a social shaping of technology perspective, we studied evidence on the socio-technical forces that shape OA publishing practices. We examined a variety of data sources, including, but not limited to, publisher policies and guidelines, OA mandates and policies and author surveys. 
 Results: Over the last three decades, scholarly publishing has experienced a shift from “closed” access to OA as the proportion of scholarly literature that is openly accessible has increased continuously. Estimated OA levels for publication years after 2010 varied between 29.4% and 66%. The shift towards OA is uneven across disciplines in two respects: first, the growth of OA has been uneven across disciplines, which manifests itself in varying OA prevalence levels. Second, disciplines use different OA publishing channels to make research outputs OA. 
 Conclusions: We conclude that historically rooted publishing practices differ in terms of their compatibility with OA, which is the reason why OA can be assumed to be a natural continuation of publishing cultures in some disciplines, whereas in other disciplines, the implementation of OA faces major barriers and would require a change of research culture.
review_content:
I’m sorry that I haven’t been slow with reviewing this study, but the increasing length of studies, which generally I think necessary, makes peer review even more onerous.

Importance:
  * The study asks two important questions - what is the variation in use of open access by discipline, and what might be the reasons for the differences? And it provides answers that are generally convincing, although hard to digest.

Originality:
  * Individual studies provide some answers to these questions, but this review brings them together. That is useful.

Methods and presentation:
  * Although the study is described as a meta-synthesis, it seems to me that it’s essentially a descriptive study. The authors find the studies and then largely describe what they report. There isn’t much synthesis, and I, as a reader, would appreciate more.
  * There is huge heterogeneity in the studies of proportions of articles that are open access, but readers are left to look through a table that is four pages long - and largely to wonder for themselves about the reasons for the big variations. I know that all the data are there, but how is it that a study of 12m article from 2018 finds that 66% of articles are open access, whereas another equally large study from the same year finds that 29% are open access? Clearly they must be using different definitions of open access, and the authors don’t themselves define open access or its subsets (gold, green, hybrid, and bronze). They should. I’d like to see a summary table that has the following columns: Year of study, number of articles in the study, definition of open access, proportion of articles that were open access.
  * There should be another summary table that shows the variation by discipline in overall open access rates and in the subsets of open access.
  * Another useful addition would be a figure that showed how proportions of articles that are open access by discipline have varied over time.
  * The authors might also give a table that shows the association between their “analytical dimension” and the different disciplines. At the moment readers can get this information only by ploughing through pages of text that describe the variations by discipline.
  * As this is essentially a descriptive study I don’t have great criticisms of the methods and conclusions, although I recognise the weakness of surveys, which give us data on what people say about their behaviour than what really drives their behaviour.
  * My biggest criticisms are about presentation. I’d like to see not only more tables and a figure but also a much shorter paper backed up by supplementary material if necessary. That would, I judge, make for a much more readable and useful paper and dramatically increase the number of readers.

Minor points:
  * There is at the moment a great deal of repetition. The discussion is mostly a repetition of the results.
  * I’d like to see some data in the abstract.
  * I believe that abbreviations are a plague in medical writing, and I’d avoid them, including OA for open access.
  * I’d drop “evidence-based” in the title.
  * It would be good to have the search strategy as a table.
  * Much of what’s in the results should ideally be in the discussion.
  * There are a fair few typos.
paper_title_zh: 学科特定的开放获取出版实践及变革障碍：基于证据的综述
paper_abstract_zh:
背景：围绕开放获取（OA）的许多讨论都集中在它如何影响不同学术领域的出版实践上。长期以来，人们普遍认为，所有学科全面且相对同质性地实施OA只是时间问题。然而，近期的大规模文献计量研究表明，OA的采用在不同学科之间存在显著差异。我们旨在回答两个问题：首先，不同学科如何采纳和塑造OA出版实践？其次，可以识别出哪些学科特定的OA障碍和潜力？

方法：首先，我们识别并综合了评估各学科OA普及率和出版模式的相关文献计量研究。其次，采用技术社会塑造视角，我们研究了塑造OA出版实践的社会技术力量的证据。我们审查了多种数据来源，包括但不限于出版商政策和指南、OA指令和政策以及作者调查。

结果：在过去三十年中，学术出版经历了从“封闭”获取到OA的转变，因为公开可获取的学术文献比例持续增加。2010年以后的出版年份估计OA水平介于29.4%至66%之间。向OA的转变在学科间不均衡，体现在两个方面：首先，OA的增长在不同学科间不均衡，表现为不同的OA普及率水平。其次，学科使用不同的OA出版渠道来使研究成果开放获取。

结论：我们认为，历史上根深蒂固的出版实践在与其与OA的兼容性方面存在差异，这就是为什么可以假设OA是一些学科出版文化的自然延续，而在其他学科中，OA的实施面临重大障碍，并需要改变研究文化的原因。
review_content_zh:
很抱歉我并未拖延评审这项研究，但研究篇幅的不断增加（我认为这通常是必要的）使得同行评审变得更加繁重。

重要性：
  * 该研究提出了两个重要问题——各学科在开放获取使用上的差异是什么，以及这些差异可能的原因是什么？它提供的答案总体上是令人信服的，尽管难以消化。

原创性：
  * 单个研究对这些问题提供了一些答案，但这项综述将它们整合在一起。这是有用的。

方法和呈现：
  * 尽管该研究被描述为元综合，但在我看来，它本质上是一项描述性研究。作者找到这些研究，然后主要描述了它们报告的内容。综合的部分并不多，作为读者，我希望看到更多。
  * 在开放获取文章比例的研究中存在巨大的异质性，但读者需要浏览一个长达四页的表格——并且主要靠自己揣摩这些巨大差异的原因。我知道所有数据都在那里，但一项关于2018年1200万篇文章的研究发现66%的文章是开放获取的，而同年另一项同样规模的研究却发现29%的文章是开放获取的。显然，它们必须使用了不同的开放获取定义，而作者们自己并未定义开放获取及其子集（金色、绿色、混合和青铜）。他们应该这样做。我希望看到一个包含以下列的总结表格：研究年份、研究中的文章数量、开放获取的定义、开放获取文章的比例。
  * 应该有另一个总结表格，展示各学科在总体开放获取率和开放获取子集方面的差异。
  * 另一个有用的补充是一张图，展示各学科开放获取文章比例随时间的变化。
  * 作者们还可以提供一个表格，展示他们的“分析维度”与不同学科之间的关联。目前，读者只能通过翻阅描述各学科差异的文本页面来获取这些信息。
  * 由于这本质上是一项描述性研究，我对方法和结论没有大的批评，尽管我认识到调查的弱点，它们提供的是关于人们对其行为的说法，而非真正驱动其行为的数据。
  * 我最大的批评在于呈现方式。我希望看到的不仅是有更多的表格和图表，而且是一篇更短的论文，如有必要，辅以补充材料。我认为这将使论文更加易读和有用，并显著增加读者数量。

次要问题：
  * 目前存在大量重复。讨论部分大多是结果的重复。
  * 我希望摘要中能看到一些数据。
  * 我认为缩写在医学写作中是一种祸害，我会避免使用它们，包括用OA表示开放获取。
  * 我会去掉标题中的“基于证据的”。
  * 将搜索策略以表格形式呈现会更好。
  * 结果中的许多内容理想情况下应该放在讨论部分。
  * 有相当多的错别字。

reasons: For the most part, yes, but I do think the strictness of the criteria for the systemic literature review of OA uptake requires that supplementing research that is left out of the review is still discussed/reflected upon as in some other parts of the manuscript.

One source which I think is a great omission and gives a lot of detailed breakdown into the differences between OA journal differences is: Crawford, W. (2018). GOAJ3: Gold Open Access Journals 2012-2017. https://walt.lishost.org/2018/05/goaj3-gold-open-access-journals-2012-2017/.

If “top-down” studies, focusing on only one type of OA mechanism, were excluded this study was perhaps not included on such grounds but I think it is doing the study a disservice – there is no better source that describes the disciplinary differences longitudinally across disciplines, including information about article processing charges, than that e-book and associated dataset.
If not integrated into the meta-analysis it should at least be used in the other parts of the manuscript to frame the study and its results.
Further reference you could consider, purely based on the idea that they have also explored disciplinary differences in the OA context specifically, albeit through analysis of bibliographic indexes:

In general I avoid suggesting citing material that I have been involved in authoring as part of reviews I have conducted, but in this case I would like to point out two studies that give precise metrics of various types of OA in narrowly defined disciplines, and another study which deals with disciplinary differences in self-archiving rights, utilizing these references is completely optional and not something that influences my verdict or recommendation for a revised version of the paper:

The influence of academic social networks is in my view underrepresented in the review of existing literature and conclusions of the study, they have provided a substantial share of the OA copies measured in the various bibliometric studies and many authors also perceive them as essentially “solving” the issue of OA and paywalls on a personal level since there has been very weak monitoring of adherence to copyright on such services.
The concept of Bronze OA would need further unpacking since in most of the reviewed studies it is present, but not always separated and referred to as such from other OA provision mechanisms.

For me it was a bit unclear what the first criteria in Table 1 when strictly applied entails, do the studies have to explore OA availability “bottom-up” through web-search engines/querying and giving uptake metrics for various OA mechanisms in one single study?
I’d like to see a summary table that has the following columns: Year of study, number of articles in the study, definition of open access, proportion of articles that were open access.
There should be another summary table that shows the variation by discipline in overall open access rates and in the subsets of open access.
Another useful addition would be a figure that showed how proportions of articles that are open access by discipline have varied over time.
The authors might also give a table that shows the association between their “analytical dimension” and the different disciplines.
At the moment readers can get this information only by ploughing through pages of text that describe the variations by discipline.
Much of what’s in the results should ideally be in the discussion.
It would be good to have the search strategy as a table.
The discussion is mostly a repetition of the results.

paper_title: ERCP-induced perforation: review and revisit after half a century
paper_abstract:
Background 
    Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is an invasive procedure. We aimed to investigate ERCP-induced perforations at our institution and conduct a comprehensive review of literature on ERCP-induced perforations (EIP) since the introduction of this procedure as a therapeutic intervention. 
  
  
    Methods 
    This was a case-control study, in which charts of all patients diagnosed with ERCP-induced duodenal perforation were reviewed and compared to a control group without perforation. Patient’s sociodemographic and clinical data, including ERCP procedure-related data, were gathered. 
  
  
    Results 
    A total of 996 ERCP procedures were performed; only 13 patients proved to have EIP. Obstructive jaundice was the most common indication for ERCP. The main predisposing factor was difficult cannulation (P = 0.003). In total, five patients required surgical treatment; the majority of them had type I perforation, whereas type IV was the most common in patients who were treated conservatively. The overall mortality rate was 15%, the surgical group had a slightly higher mortality rate. 
  
  
    Conclusions 
    Fifty years after the introduction of ERCP for therapy, it remains an invasive procedure that carries significant morbidity and mortality, even in skilled hands or at high- volume units. Conservative management of perforation yields favorable outcomes in selected patients.

paper_title_zh: ERCP诱导的穿孔：半个世纪后的回顾与再探
paper_abstract_zh:
背景
内镜逆行胆胰管造影（ERCP）是一种侵入性手术。我们旨在调查我院ERCP引发的穿孔情况，并对自该手术作为治疗干预手段引入以来关于ERCP引发穿孔（EIP）的文献进行全面回顾。

方法
这是一项病例对照研究，回顾了所有诊断为ERCP引发十二指肠穿孔的患者的病历，并与无穿孔的对照组进行比较。收集了患者的社会人口学和临床数据，包括与ERCP手术相关的数据。

结果
共进行了996例ERCP手术；仅13例患者证实为EIP。阻塞性黄疸是ERCP最常见的指征。主要易感因素是困难插管（P = 0.003）。共有5例患者需要手术治疗；其中大多数为I型穿孔，而IV型在保守治疗的患者中最常见。总体死亡率为15%，手术组的死亡率略高。

结论
ERCP作为治疗手段引入50年后，它仍然是一种侵入性手术，即使在技术娴熟的操作者或高容量单位中，也伴随着显著的发病率和死亡率。对选定的患者进行穿孔的保守管理可获得良好预后。

paper_title: The application of plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria in Solanum lycopersicum production in the agricultural system: A review
paper_abstract: Food safety is a significant challenge worldwide, from plantation to cultivation, especially for perishable products such as tomatoes. New eco-friendly strategies are needed, and beneficial microorganisms might be a sustainable solution. This study demonstrates bacteria activity in the tomato plant rhizosphere. Further, it investigates the rhizobacteria's structure, function, and diversity in soil. Rhizobacteria that promote the growth and development of tomato plants are referred to as plant growth-promoting bacteria (PGPR). They form a series of associations with plants and other organisms in the soil through a mutualistic relationship where both parties benefit from living together. It implies the antagonistic activities of the rhizobacteria to deter pathogens from invading tomato plants through their roots. Some PGPR are regarded as biological control agents that hinder the development of spoilage organisms and can act as an alternative for agricultural chemicals that may be detrimental to the health of humans, animals, and some of the beneficial microbes in the rhizosphere soil. These bacteria also help tomato plants acquire essential nutrients like K, Mg, P, and N. Some rhizobacteria may offer a solution to low tomato production and help tackle food insecurity and farming problems. In this review, an overview of soil-inhabiting rhizobacteria focused on improving the sustainable production of Solanum lycopersicum.

paper_title: Data Distillation: A Survey
paper_abstract: The popularity of deep learning has led to the curation of a vast number of massive and multifarious datasets. Despite having close-to-human performance on individual tasks, training parameter-hungry models on large datasets poses multi-faceted problems such as (a) high model-training time; (b) slow research iteration; and (c) poor eco-sustainability. As an alternative, data distillation approaches aim to synthesize terse data summaries, which can serve as effective drop-in replacements of the original dataset for scenarios like model training, inference, architecture search, etc. In this survey, we present a formal framework for data distillation, along with providing a detailed taxonomy of existing approaches. Additionally, we cover data distillation approaches for different data modalities, namely images, graphs, and user-item interactions (recommender systems), while also identifying current challenges and future research directions.
review_content:
**Summary Of Contributions:**
This paper is a review on Data Distillation, which aims to reduce the size of datasets of various learning tasks and synthesize terse data summaries that can be used as alternatives for modeling training/inference. The paper begins by presenting the concept and rationale behind data distillation. Subsequently, it delves into a thorough examination of five primary categories of data distillation methods. Furthermore, the paper explores the modality and application of data distillation, providing valuable insights. Lastly, it outlines several prospective directions for future research in this field.

**Strengths And Weaknesses:**
Strengths: 1. The topic discussed in the paper is highly significant, especially in the context of the prevalence of large-scale models today. With the escalating costs associated with model training, utilizing data distillation to expedite both training and inference processes is very important. This review has the potential to advance this objective. 2. The paper provides a concise and accurate summary of the existing five data distillation methods. It includes a comprehensive summary of primary references and offers method descriptions that are not only mathematically rigorous but also provide sufficient details. 3. The future directions outlined in Section 5 are valuable references for subsequent research in the field. 4. The paper is well-organized and written-well. Weaknesses: 1. It seems that the paper only focused on labeled datasets. However, regarding tasks without annotations, such as unconditioned image synthesis, are there any works related to data distillation? 2. Currently, large-scale models and datasets are highly popular. Could the author summarize if there are any data distillation methods specifically designed for large datasets? 3. On Page 3, below Definition 3, the paper highlights three key criteria for evaluating data distillation methods: performance, efficiency, and transferability. I'm curious if robustness should be considered as a fourth criterion. For instance, when training with a distilled dataset, is the model more vonerable to adversarial attack methods? 4. An important role of data distillation is to boost training. Could the author provide a summary of the existing methods and their impact on training speed improvement?

**Requested Changes:**
Please attempt to address the concerns within the "Weakness" section.

**Broader Impact Concerns:**
I have no concerns on the broader impact.

**Claims And Evidence:**
Yes

**Audience:**
Yes

**Rebuttal Comments:**
Response to questions raised: We sincerely thank the reviewer for the time and effort in reviewing our paper and providing valuable feedback. We address each of the pointed weaknesses below: 1. You’re right — all existing data distillation techniques are designed for classification tasks, and developing data distillation techniques suitable for other predictive tasks (e.g., generation) is a promising future direction. Since there exists no work on data distillation for non-classification settings, we have already listed this direction (in addition to others) in the “New data modalities & settings” discussion in “Section 5: Challenges & Future Directions”. 2. While this is another promising direction for future research that is unexplored, existing techniques are limited to only the smaller academic datasets (e.g., CIFAR10, ImageNet subsets). We already hint toward this mismatch in the “Better scaling” discussion in “Section 5: Challenges & Future Directions”, but to make the connection more clear, we will reframe this in our next revision. 3. Thanks for the suggestion — it would indeed be an interesting idea to evaluate the synthesized data’s robustness. We promise to include a new discussion on “Robust data quality evaluation” in “Section 5: Challenges & Future Directions”. 4. While one of the major merits to data distillation is indeed to accelerate model training, existing work doesn’t explicitly mention the training speedup, simply because of a $1:1$ train-time speedup relative to the size of the training dataset. For example, if we distill CIFAR10’s train-set ($50k$ images) into a data summary of 10 images per class ($\equiv10\times10$ total images), we will observe a $\frac{50\cdot10^3}{100} = 500\times$ train-time speedup as the underlying original vs. distilled image size is the same. Since this seems like an important point to note, we will clarify this $1:1$ correlation in Section 2.
paper_title_zh: 数据蒸馏：综述
paper_abstract_zh: 深度学习的普及导致了大量多样化数据集的编纂。尽管在单个任务上具有接近人类的性能，但在大型数据集上训练参数密集型模型带来了多方面的问题，例如：(a) 模型训练时间长；(b) 研究迭代缓慢；(c) 生态可持续性差。作为一种替代方案，数据蒸馏方法旨在合成简洁的数据摘要，这些摘要可以作为模型训练、推理、架构搜索等场景中原始数据集的有效替代品。在这篇综述中，我们提出了一个数据蒸馏的正式框架，并提供了现有方法的详细分类。此外，我们还涵盖了不同数据模态的数据蒸馏方法，即图像、图和用户-物品交互（推荐系统），同时识别了当前挑战和未来研究方向。
review_content_zh:
**贡献总结：**
本文是对数据蒸馏的综述，旨在减少各种学习任务数据集的大小，并合成简洁的数据摘要，这些摘要可作为建模训练/推理的替代品。文章首先介绍了数据蒸馏的概念和原理。随后，深入探讨了五类主要的数据蒸馏方法。此外，文章还探讨了数据蒸馏的模态和应用，提供了宝贵的见解。最后，概述了该领域未来研究的几个潜在方向。

**优点与不足：**
优点：1. 文章讨论的主题非常重要，尤其是在当今大规模模型普及的背景下。随着模型训练成本的不断上升，利用数据蒸馏加速训练和推理过程至关重要。本综述有望推动这一目标。2. 文章对现有的五种数据蒸馏方法进行了简洁而准确的总结，包括主要参考文献的全面概述，并提供不仅在数学上严谨且细节充分的方法描述。3. 第5节中概述的未来方向为该领域的后续研究提供了宝贵的参考。4. 文章组织良好，写作质量高。
不足：1. 文章似乎只关注了有标签的数据集。然而，对于无注释的任务，如无条件图像合成，是否有与数据蒸馏相关的工作？2. 目前，大规模模型和数据集非常流行。作者能否总结是否有针对大型数据集专门设计的数据蒸馏方法？3. 在第3页，定义3下方，文章强调了评估数据蒸馏方法的三个关键标准：性能、效率和可迁移性。我好奇是否应将鲁棒性作为第四个标准。例如，使用蒸馏数据集训练时，模型是否更容易受到对抗攻击方法的影响？4. 数据蒸馏的一个重要角色是提升训练速度。作者能否总结现有方法及其对训练速度提升的影响？

**请求的修改：**
请尝试解决“不足”部分中提出的问题。

**更广泛影响关切：**
我对更广泛的影响没有关切。

**主张与证据：**
是

**受众：**
是

**反驳意见：**
对提出问题的回应：我们衷心感谢审稿人抽出时间和精力审阅我们的论文并提供宝贵的反馈。我们针对每个指出的不足进行回应：1. 您是对的——所有现有的数据蒸馏技术都是为分类任务设计的，开发适用于其他预测任务（例如，生成）的数据蒸馏技术是一个有前景的未来方向。由于目前尚无针对非分类设置的数据蒸馏工作，我们已经在“第5节：挑战与未来方向”中的“新数据模态与设置”讨论中列出了这一方向（以及其他方向）。2. 虽然这是未来研究的另一个有前景但未探索的方向，但现有技术仅限于较小的学术数据集（例如，CIFAR10，ImageNet子集）。我们已经在“第5节：挑战与未来方向”中的“更好扩展”讨论中暗示了这种不匹配，但为了使联系更清晰，我们将在下一次修订中重新表述这一点。3. 感谢您的建议——评估合成数据的鲁棒性确实是一个有趣的想法。我们承诺在“第5节：挑战与未来方向”中增加关于“鲁棒数据质量评估”的新讨论。4. 虽然数据蒸馏的主要优点之一确实是加速模型训练，但现有工作并未明确提及训练速度提升，仅仅是因为与训练数据集大小有$1:1$的训练时间加速关系。例如，如果我们将CIFAR10的训练集（$50k$图像）蒸馏成每类10个图像的数据摘要（$\equiv10\times10$总图像），我们将观察到$\frac{50\cdot10^3}{100} = 500\times$的训练时间加速，因为底层原始与蒸馏图像大小相同。由于这似乎是一个重要的注意点，我们将在第2节中澄清这一$1:1$的相关性。

paper_title: Quality of information in news media reports about the effects of health interventions: Systematic review and meta-analyses
paper_abstract:
Background 
Many studies have assessed the quality of news reports about the effects of health interventions, but there has been no systematic review of such studies or meta-analysis of their results. We aimed to fill this gap (PROSPERO ID: CRD42018095032). 
 Methods 
We included studies that used at least one explicit, prespecified and generic criterion to assess the quality of news reports in print, broadcast, or online news media, and specified the sampling frame, and the selection criteria and technique. We assessed criteria individually for inclusion in the meta-analyses, excluding ineligible criteria and criteria with inadequately reported results. We mapped and grouped criteria to facilitate evidence synthesis. Where possible, we extracted the proportion of news reports meeting the included criterion. We performed meta-analyses using a random effects model to estimate such proportions for individual criteria and some criteria groups, and to characterise heterogeneity across studies.  
 Results 
We included 44 primary studies in the review, and 18 studies and 108 quality criteria in the meta-analyses. Many news reports gave an unbalanced and oversimplified picture of the potential consequences of interventions. A limited number mention or adequately address conflicts of interest (22%; 95% CI 7%-49%) (low certainty), alternative interventions (36%; 95% CI 26%-47%) (moderate certainty), potential harms (40%; 95% CI 23%-61%) (low certainty), or costs (18%; 95% CI 12%-28%) (moderate certainty), or quantify effects (53%; 95% CI 36%-69%) (low certainty) or report absolute effects (17%; 95% CI 4%-49%) (low certainty).  
 Discussion 
There is room for improving health news, but it is logically more important to improve the public’s ability to critically appraise health information and make judgements for themselves.
review_content:
The other reviewers of this article have highlighted its considerable strengths and I won’t repeat their comments. This is a solid attempt to summarise studies that have made structured attempts to quantify and report key characteristics of medical news stories that report therapeutic claims. It is very useful to have this summary.

Many of these studies were carried out to highlight the weaknesses in the reporting of medical advances in the mainstream media in the hope that this would raise standards. But there is no strong evidence that this has resulted from these efforts.

The studies included in this review preceded the news coverage of COVID-19, its preventive and therapeutic interventions. It would be very instructive to measure how the media performed during the epidemic and whether reporting evolved. My informal impression is that respect for science, and possibly the reports themselves, have improved. However, this has been countered by ignorant and some willfully and politically motivated inaccurate reporting in a few mainstream outlets and social media. My point is that the media landscape may have changed because of Covid-19.

I only have a few specific comments:
 1. I don’t think that conventional meta-analysis produces meaningful data in this situation. Meta-analysis is at its best when we can assume that there is an underlying single effect of interest that is measured imprecisely by individual studies. For instance, the relative effects of many important medications (e.g, statins, anticoagulants), which seem constant across different settings and background risks. Meta-estimates of prevalence are less helpful as there is usually an assumed variation. That is the case here where the study methods, story topics, settings, and reporters vary. There is no reason to assume a common effect to be meta-analysed. Some of the I2 values are huge. In my view it would be preferable to present more as a scoping review, displaying and discussing the range of values reported by the studies.
 2. The investigators, appropriately, have mapped the varying scales and items to a common framework. They have used their own Informed Health Choices (IHC) Key Concepts framework. That’s fine, but the paper seems to assume a familiarity with the framework that many readers will not possess. I think a simplified version of the framework needs to be presented in the main text. At present, it seems to be buried in Supplementary data.
 3. In the Abstract, the authors conclude: ‘There is room for improving health news, but it is logically more important to improve the public’s ability to critically appraise health information and make judgements for themselves.’ The paper does not provide data to support this conclusion. The authors have done important ground-breaking work with IHC but the extensive coverage they provide themselves in the Discussion of an already long paper seems excessive. A separate editorial/opinion piece making these points would be welcome.
 4. I think there may be a mistake in the dot point summary in the Discussion which states ‘• 86% of news reports commit “disease mongering” (95% CI 78%-91%) (low certainty).’ In the paper they state ‘Overall, 86% of news reports do not commit disease mongering (95% CI 78%-91%)’. I think the latter is correct.
paper_title_zh: 新闻媒体报道中关于健康干预效果信息质量的系统评价与荟萃分析
paper_abstract_zh:
背景
许多研究评估了关于健康干预效果新闻报道的质量，但尚未有对这些研究的系统综述或其结果的元分析。我们旨在填补这一空白（PROSPERO ID: CRD42018095032）。

方法
我们纳入了使用至少一个明确、预先指定且通用的标准来评估印刷、广播或在线新闻媒体中新闻报道质量的研究，并指定了抽样框架、选择标准和技术。我们逐个评估标准以纳入元分析，排除了不合格的标准和结果报告不充分的标准。我们将标准进行映射和分组，以促进证据综合。在可能的情况下，我们提取了符合所包含标准的新闻报道比例。我们使用随机效应模型进行元分析，以估计单个标准及某些标准组的此类比例，并描述研究间的异质性。

结果
我们纳入了44项原始研究进行综述，并在元分析中纳入了18项研究和108个质量标准。许多新闻报道对干预潜在后果的描述不平衡且过于简化。仅有少数提及或充分处理了利益冲突（22%；95% CI 7%-49%）（低确定性）、替代干预（36%；95% CI 26%-47%）（中等确定性）、潜在危害（40%；95% CI 23%-61%）（低确定性）或成本（18%；95% CI 12%-28%）（中等确定性），或量化效果（53%；95% CI 36%-69%）（低确定性）或报告绝对效果（17%；95% CI 4%-49%）（低确定性）。

讨论
健康新闻有改进的空间，但逻辑上更重要的是提高公众批判性评估健康信息并为自己做出判断的能力。
review_content_zh:
其他审稿人已强调了本文的显著优点，我将不再重复他们的评论。这是一次扎实的尝试，旨在总结那些结构化地量化并报告了含有治疗声明的医学新闻故事关键特征的研究。拥有这样的总结非常有用。

许多这类研究旨在突出主流媒体在报道医学进展方面的弱点，希望借此提高报道标准。然而，没有强有力的证据表明这些努力已产生如此结果。

本综述所包含的研究先于对COVID-19及其预防和治疗干预的新闻报道。衡量媒体在疫情期间的表现以及报道是否有所改进，将极具启发性。我的非正式印象是，对科学的尊重，以及可能报道本身，都有所提升。然而，这一进步被一些主流媒体和社交媒体中的无知报道以及某些有意为之且受政治动机驱使的不准确报道所抵消。我的观点是，媒体格局可能因COVID-19而发生了变化。

我只有几点具体意见：
1. 我认为在这种情况下，传统的元分析不会产生有意义的数据。当我们可以假设存在一个单一的兴趣效应，且该效应被各个研究不精确地测量时，元分析最为有效。例如，许多重要药物（如他汀类药物、抗凝剂）的相对效应，在不同环境和背景风险中似乎保持恒定。而流行率的元估计较少有帮助，因为通常存在假设的变异。在本研究中，研究方法、故事主题、环境和报道者各不相同。没有理由假设存在一个共同的效应以进行元分析。一些I²值非常大。在我看来，最好将其呈现为范围综述，展示并讨论各研究报道的数值范围。
2. 研究人员适当地将不同的量表和项目映射到一个共同框架上。他们使用了自有的“知情健康选择”（IHC）关键概念框架。这没问题，但论文似乎假定读者对该框架已有所了解，而许多读者并不具备这种了解。我认为需要在正文部分呈现该框架的简化版本。目前，它似乎被埋没在补充数据中。
3. 在摘要中，作者总结道：“健康新闻有改进空间，但从逻辑上讲，更重要的是提高公众批判性评估健康信息并自行做出判断的能力。”论文未提供支持这一结论的数据。作者在IHC方面做了重要的开创性工作，但在已很长的论文讨论部分中对自己工作的广泛覆盖似乎过多。一篇单独的社论/观点文章来阐述这些观点将更受欢迎。
4. 我认为讨论部分的要点总结中可能存在错误，其中写道：“• 86%的新闻报道存在‘疾病贩卖’（95% CI 78%-91%）（低确定性）。”而在论文中他们写道：“总体而言，86%的新闻报道未进行疾病贩卖（95% CI 78%-91%）。”我认为后者是正确的。

reasons: Search strategy: It seems almost 2 years since it was updated.
Authors might consider updating before indexing.
The authors have done important ground-breaking work with IHC but the extensive coverage they provide themselves in the Discussion of an already long paper seems excessive.

86% of news reports commit “disease mongering” (95% CI 78%-91%) (low certainty).’ In the paper they state ‘Overall, 86% of news reports do not commit disease mongering (95% CI 78%-91%)’. I think the latter is correct.

paper_title: The role of connective tissue in the embryology of the musculoskeletal system: towards a paradigm shift
paper_abstract: This paper presents a review of literature regarding the role of embryological connective tissue in the formation of muscles and the organization of the musculoskeletal system. The intention is to introduce a potential paradigm shift with regards to understanding peripheral coordination of movement and movement patterns. This new perspective could improve comprehension of the normal physiological function of connective tissue and, whenever it is pathological, resultant symptoms. Furthermore, this paper briefly discusses some implications of this paradigm shift in the interpretation of movement patterns, posing further questions for future research.
review_content:
This review sets out to challenge current thinking on the role of connective tissue. This is at its clearest in the “New questions for research” section where several concepts are listed that might guide new research or the interpretation of older research. Unfortunately the preceding text does not delineate with sufficient clarity or precision the context of potentially antiquated concepts or emerging ideas that would make these questions for new research seem important or relevant to the reader. Indeed, the promise in the title that this article will address a “paradigm shift” is simply not matched by a clear explanation of what old paradigm(s) are being questioned or what new paradigm(s) are being proposed. An explicit and specific synopsis of what concepts are being challenged and proposed is urgently needed and should appear prominently in the Abstract and/or Introduction and should perhaps be reiterated in the Discussion and/or Conclusion.

More explicit and conventional organization would benefit the article in other ways. While there is a titled section on “Anatomy and physiology”, the preceding text devoted to embryology falls in the titled “Introduction” section. This lack of symmetry and the immediate launch into embryological detail under the “Introduction” heading is confusing. Then there is a “Discussion” section in which the literature review continues, rather than switching to an overview or synthesis of what was presented in earlier sections, as normally occurs in a Discussion section. This inconsistent and non-conventional use of titled sections detracts from the article’s sense of focus and direction.

Finally, there are a couple of needed improvements in the discussion of early development. 1) There are several Spanish words retained in Figure 2 where the following changes are needed: Corda to Chorda; Cefalic to Cephalic; Esclerotomo to Sclerotome; Miotomo to Myotome; Dermotomo to Dermatome. 2) The text discusses mesenchyme as a “special section” on the “sides of the paraxial mesoderm.” But the term “mesenchyme” does not appear in Figure 2. I think it would be more correct and more in line with Figure 2, to say that the mesenchyme (with the exception of head mesenchyme) is derived from or formed from lateral plate mesoderm (or “a special section flanking the paraxial mesoderm”) rather than defining it is an initial subdivision of the mesoderm.
paper_title_zh: 结缔组织在肌肉骨骼系统胚胎学中的作用：迈向范式转变
paper_abstract_zh: 本文综述了关于胚胎结缔组织在肌肉形成和肌肉骨骼系统组织中的作用的相关文献。旨在引入关于理解运动的外周协调和运动模式的潜在范式转变。这一新视角可以提升对结缔组织正常生理功能的理解，以及在病理状态下所导致症状的认识。此外，本文简要讨论了这一范式转变在运动模式解读中的一些影响，并为未来的研究提出了进一步的问题。
review_content_zh:
本文旨在挑战当前关于结缔组织角色的思考。这在“新研究问题”部分最为明确，其中列举了几个可能指导新研究或解释旧研究的概念。然而，前文并未以足够的清晰度和精确度界定那些可能过时的概念或新兴思想的背景，使得这些新研究问题对读者显得重要或相关。事实上，标题中承诺本文将探讨“范式转变”，但文中并未清晰解释哪些旧范式受到质疑，或哪些新范式被提出。迫切需要明确且具体地概述哪些概念正在被挑战和提出，这一点应在摘要和/或引言中显著呈现，并可能在讨论和/或结论中重申。

更明确和传统的组织结构将在其他方面使文章受益。虽然有一个名为“解剖学与生理学”的章节，但前文关于胚胎学的部分却放在了名为“引言”的章节中。这种不对称性以及直接在“引言”标题下展开胚胎学细节的做法令人困惑。接着是一个“讨论”部分，其中文献综述仍在继续，而不是像通常在讨论部分那样转向对前文内容的概述或综合。这种不一致和非传统的标题使用方式削弱了文章的聚焦感和方向感。

最后，关于早期发育的讨论中有几处需要改进的地方。1）图2中保留了几个西班牙语词汇，需要进行以下更改：Corda改为Chorda；Cefalic改为Cephalic；Esclerotomo改为Sclerotome；Miotomo改为Myotome；Dermotomo改为Dermatome。2）文本中将间充质描述为“轴旁中胚层侧面”的“特殊部分”。但“间充质”一词并未出现在图2中。我认为更准确且更符合图2的说法是，间充质（头部间充质除外）源自或形成于侧板中胚层（或“轴旁中胚层侧面的特殊部分”），而不是将其定义为中胚层的初始亚分区。

paper_title: Association between angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) gene I/D polymorphism with the risk of knee OA: A systematic review, meta-analysis, and meta-regression
paper_abstract:
Background 
     Previous studies have linked genetics to knee osteoarthritis. Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) gene I/D polymorphism may cause OA. However, evidence remains inconsistent. This study examines knee OA risk and ACE gene I/D polymorphism. 
   
   
     Methods 
     We explored Europe PMC, Medline, Scopus, and Cochrane Library using keywords. Three assessment bias factors were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). Criteria for inclusion: (1) Split the study population into knee OA patients and healthy controls; (2) Analysed the ACE gene I/D polymorphism; (3) Case-control or cross-sectional surveys. Studies with non-knee OA, incomplete data, and no full-text were excluded. The odds ratio (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CI) were calculated using random-effect models. 
   
   
     Results 
     A total of 6 case-control studies consist of 1,226 patients with knee OA and 1,145 healthy subjects as controls were included. Our pooled analysis revealed that a significant association between ACE gene I/D polymorphism and risk of knee OA was only seen in the dominant (DD + ID vs. II) [OR 1.69 (95% CI 1.14 – 2.50), p = 0.009, I2 = 72%], and ID vs. II [OR 1.37 (95% CI 1.01– 1.86), p = 0.04, I2 = 43%] genotype models. Other genotype models, including recessive (DD vs. ID + II), alleles (D vs. I), DD vs. ID, and DD vs. II models did not show a significant association with knee OA risk. Further regression analysis revealed that ethnicity and sex may influence those relationships in several genotype models. 
   
   
     Conclusions 
     Dominant and ID vs. II ACE gene I/D polymorphism models increased knee OA risk significantly. More research with larger samples and different ethnic groups is needed to confirm our findings. After ethnicity subgroup analysis, some genetic models in our study showed significant heterogeneities, and most studies are from Asian countries with Asian populations, with little evidence on Arabs.
review_content:
Major comment:
The study's results are significant in that they contribute to the understanding of the genetic factors involved in the development of knee OA and may have implications for the prevention and treatment of the disease. However, there are some data that need clarification:
1. **Sample Size Discrepancy**: The total number of samples is reported as 2,371 in the study selection and characteristics subsection, but as 2,367 in the classical model subsection.
2. **Focus on Results and Implications**: The authors should also explore how factors interact with the ACE gene I/D polymorphism to influence the outcomes of knee OA. This would provide a more comprehensive understanding of the genetic and environmental factors involved in the disease.

Minor comment:
This manuscript presents a comprehensive analysis of the relationship between the angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) gene I/D polymorphism and the risk of knee osteoarthritis (OA). The meta-analysis was well written according to the PRISMA guidelines. The authors also provide a comprehensive summary of the existing literature on the topic, highlighting the strengths and limitations of previous studies
paper_title_zh: 血管紧张素转换酶（ACE）基因I/D多态性与膝骨关节炎风险的相关性：系统评价、荟萃分析和荟萃回归
paper_abstract_zh:
背景
先前的研究将遗传因素与膝骨关节炎联系起来。血管紧张素转换酶（ACE）基因I/D多态性可能导致骨关节炎。然而，证据仍不一致。本研究考察了膝骨关节炎风险与ACE基因I/D多态性的关系。

方法
我们使用关键词在Europe PMC、Medline、Scopus和Cochrane Library中进行了搜索。使用Newcastle-Ottawa Scale（NOS）评估了三个评估偏差因素。纳入标准：（1）将研究人群分为膝骨关节炎患者和健康对照；（2）分析ACE基因I/D多态性；（3）病例对照或横断面调查。排除非膝骨关节炎、数据不完整和无全文的研究。使用随机效应模型计算了优势比（OR）和95%置信区间（95% CI）。

结果
共纳入6项病例对照研究，包括1,226名膝骨关节炎患者和1,145名健康对照。我们的荟萃分析显示，仅在显性（DD + ID vs. II）[OR 1.69 (95% CI 1.14 – 2.50), p = 0.009, I2 = 72%]和ID vs. II [OR 1.37 (95% CI 1.01– 1.86), p = 0.04, I2 = 43%]基因型模型中观察到ACE基因I/D多态性与膝骨关节炎风险的显著关联。其他基因型模型，包括隐性（DD vs. ID + II）、等位基因（D vs. I）、DD vs. ID和DD vs. II模型，未显示出与膝骨关节炎风险的显著关联。进一步回归分析显示，种族和性别可能影响这些关系在多个基因型模型中。

结论
显性和ID vs. II ACE基因I/D多态性模型显著增加了膝骨关节炎风险。需要更多研究，使用更大样本量和不同种族群体来证实我们的发现。在种族亚组分析后，我们研究中的一些遗传模型显示出显著的异质性，并且大多数研究来自亚洲国家，以亚洲人群为主，关于阿拉伯人的证据很少。
review_content_zh:
主要评论：
本研究的结果具有重要意义，因为它们有助于理解参与膝关节骨关节炎（OA）发展的遗传因素，并可能对疾病的预防和治疗产生影响。然而，有一些数据需要澄清：
1. **样本量差异**：在研究选择和特征部分，样本总数报告为2,371，但在经典模型部分为2,367。
2. **关注结果和影响**：作者还应探讨因素如何与ACE基因I/D多态性相互作用，从而影响膝关节OA的结局。这将提供对疾病中涉及的遗传和环境因素的更全面理解。

次要评论：
本文对血管紧张素转换酶（ACE）基因I/D多态性与膝关节骨关节炎（OA）风险之间的关系进行了全面分析。根据PRISMA指南，该荟萃分析撰写得很好。作者还提供了关于该主题现有文献的全面总结，突出了先前研究的优点和局限性。

reasons: This manuscript presents a comprehensive analysis of the relationship between the angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) gene I/D polymorphism and the risk of knee osteoarthritis (OA).
The authors also provide a comprehensive summary of the existing literature on the topic, highlighting the strengths and limitations of previous studies

The study's results are significant in that they contribute to the understanding of the genetic factors involved in the development of knee OA and may have implications for the prevention and treatment of the disease.
However, there are some data that need clarification:
1. **Sample Size Discrepancy**: The total number of samples is reported as 2,371 in the study selection and characteristics subsection, but as 2,367 in the classical model subsection.

The authors should also explore how factors interact with the ACE gene I/D polymorphism to influence the outcomes of knee OA. This would provide a more comprehensive understanding of the genetic and environmental factors involved in the disease.

paper_title: Natural disaster and medication preparedness among elderly: a scoping review
paper_abstract:
Introduction 
 The increasing number of older people and their vulnerability to disaster and medication preparedness as the primary elements of disaster mitigation are necessary to reduce the impact of a disaster. Nevertheless, research on natural disasters and medication preparedness in the elderly population is still lacking. This review aimed to explore all reported research and publications related to natural disasters and medication preparedness among the elderly. 
 
 
 Methods 
 A scoping review was performed using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). A literature search was conducted using the following four databases: Scopus, PubMed, Sage, and Google Scholar. Screening was conducted using the following criteria: articles written in English, open access, and published between 2020 and 2024. Articles must discuss natural disasters and medication preparedness. In the data search, we input several keywords that include “elderly,” “natural disaster,” “preparedness,” and “medication.” Snowballing was then conducted to find articles on preparedness interventions. Data extraction and analysis were then performed. 
 
 
 Results and conclusion 
 The findings from this literature review are the majority of studies showing that most elderly people are not well prepared in facing disasters; however, through various programs that have been implemented by either the government or community, the elderly show more preparation when they encounter any natural disaster.
review_content:
Thank you for the opportunity to review this manuscript. In this paper, the authors conducted a scoping review of disaster preparedness as it relates to elderly people. I think there is some interesting information in here, and some careful re-editing and re-organization of the text could hopefully make it stronger.

General comment:

The overall quality of written English needs improvement, with many grammatical errors and overly-long descriptions in the text.

As a specific example, the opening three sentences of the main text could be re-written as “The global population of elderly people, defined as those 60 years of age or greater, is large and increasing. There were an estimated 1 billion elderly people alive in 2024, a group that is projected to grow to 1.4 billion in 2030 and 2.1 billion by 2050.” An explanation of how becoming elderly is a function of aging is not needed.

Specific comments:

Abstract – the results and conclusions are too brief; while the necessary brevity of an abstract constrains out ability to discuss results in enormous detail, some mention of the actual results of the review should be included.

Introduction – It is not necessary to mention what ministries of health are, although it is useful to mention that disaster preparedness may fail to meet the needs of older people.

Results – 5 papers out of 20 is not “most” (in reference to the number of papers that were written in the US). It is not necessary to list the journals of origin in the main text; this can be included in Table 3 and in the references.

Results – The results section does not include any actual results, just a list of papers that met their inclusion criteria. Much of this information is included in the discussion but would be properly considered part of the results. The basic organization of preparedness categories in the discussion (mobility assistance, social support, etc.) is a reasonable one, however.
paper_title_zh: 自然灾害与老年人药物准备情况：一项范围综述
paper_abstract_zh:
引言
随着老年人口数量的增加及其在灾害和药物准备方面的脆弱性，作为灾害减缓的主要要素，减少灾害影响是必要的。然而，关于老年人口在自然灾害和药物准备方面的研究仍然不足。本综述旨在探讨所有已报道的与老年人自然灾害和药物准备相关的研究和出版物。

方法
采用系统综述和荟萃分析扩展范围综述的首选报告项目（PRISMA-ScR）进行范围综述。通过以下四个数据库进行文献检索：Scopus、PubMed、Sage和Google Scholar。筛选标准如下：英文撰写、开放获取、2020年至2024年发表的文章，且必须讨论自然灾害和药物准备。在数据搜索中，我们输入了包括“老年人”、“自然灾害”、“准备”和“药物”在内的多个关键词。随后进行滚雪球法以查找有关准备干预的文章。然后进行数据提取和分析。

结果与结论
本次文献综述的发现是，大多数研究表明，大多数老年人在面对灾害时准备不足；然而，通过政府或社区实施的各种项目，老年人在遭遇任何自然灾害时表现出更多的准备。
review_content_zh:
感谢有机会审阅这篇手稿。在这篇论文中，作者对与老年人相关的灾害准备进行了范围审查。我认为这里有一些有趣的信息，经过仔细的重新编辑和文本重组，有望使其更具说服力。

总体评论：

书面英语的整体质量需要提高，文本中存在许多语法错误和过于冗长的描述。

举一个具体的例子，正文开头的三句话可以改写为：“全球老年人口，定义为60岁及以上的人群，数量庞大且在增加。据估计，2024年有10亿老年人，预计到2030年将增长到14亿，到2050年将达到21亿。”关于变老是如何衰老的一个功能解释是不必要的。

具体评论：

摘要——结果和结论过于简短；尽管摘要的必要简洁性限制了我们对结果进行详尽讨论的能力，但应提及审查的实际结果。

引言——没有必要提及卫生部门是什么，尽管提到灾害准备可能无法满足老年人的需求是有用的。

结果——20篇论文中有5篇并不代表“大多数”（指在美国撰写的论文数量）。没有必要在正文中列出期刊来源；这可以包括在表3和参考文献中。

结果——结果部分没有包含任何实际结果，只是列出了符合纳入标准的论文。许多信息包含在讨论中，但应被视为结果的一部分。然而，讨论中准备类别的基本组织（如行动辅助、社会支持等）是合理的。

reasons: 5 papers out of 20 is not “most” (in reference to the number of papers that were written in the US).
Introduction – It is not necessary to mention what ministries of health are, although it is useful to mention that disaster preparedness may fail to meet the needs of older people.
It is not necessary to list the journals of origin in the main text; this can be included in Table 3 and in the references.
I think there is some interesting information in here, and some careful re-editing and re-organization of the text could hopefully make it stronger.
Results – The results section does not include any actual results, just a list of papers that met their inclusion criteria.
Much of this information is included in the discussion but would be properly considered part of the results.
The basic organization of preparedness categories in the discussion (mobility assistance, social support, etc.) is a reasonable one, however.

paper_title: Advancing the activity cliff concept
paper_abstract: The activity cliff concept has experienced increasing interest in medicinal chemistry and chemoinformatics. Activity cliffs have originally been defined as pairs of structurally similar compounds that are active against the same target but have a large difference in potency. Activity cliffs are relevant for structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis and compound optimization because small chemical modifications can be deduced from cliffs that result in large-magnitude changes in potency. In addition to studying activity cliffs on the basis of individual compounds series, they can be systematically identified through mining of compound activity data. This commentary aims to provide a concise yet detailed picture of our current understanding of activity cliffs. It is also meant to introduce the further refined activity cliff concept to a general audience in drug development.
review_content:
This paper provides an overview of the concept of activity cliffs in structure-activity relationships and provides a number of examples of how the technique can be applied in a drug discovery setting. Activity cliffs can provide a means of better understanding the relationships between chemical structure and biological activity, as well as identifying regions of a molecule that are critical to activity. The review is directed toward the non-expert and should provide an adequate background for those unfamiliar with the topic. Those familiar with activity cliffs may want to consult more specialized reviews written by the same authors. This review is well-written, easy to follow, and provides many key references for those who would like to learn more about the topic.

The authors’ breakdown of the activity cliff concept into components will be helpful for those unfamiliar with the topic. It may be useful to point out that utilizing log differences in activity can make activity cliff scores more intuitive to chemists and biologists. Those with a limited knowledge of chemoinformatics will appreciate the discussion of fingerprint similarity. However, a figure might make these concepts even more clear. The authors' point out that "calculated fingerprint Tc values are often difficult to interpret from a medicinal chemistry point of view". In my experience, Tanimoto similarity typically makes sense, this sentence might be better as "calculated fingerprint Tc values are *sometimes* difficult to interpret". The authors mention matched molecular pairs (MMP) as a means of expressing molecular similarity.

In addition to references 12 and 13, it would be useful to include what I consider to be the seminal paper on matched molecular pairs.
Leach, A. G.; Jones, H. D.; Cosgrove, D. A.; Kenny, P. W.; Ruston,L.; MacFaul, P.; Wood, M.; Colclough, N.; Law, L. Matched Molecular Pairs as a Guide in the Optimization of Pharmaceutical Properties; A Study of Aqueous Solubility, Plasma Protein Binding and Oral Exposure. J. Med. Chem. 2006, 49, 6672–6682.

As chemists and biologists pursue more complex targets, it is necessary to increase the sophistication of our SAR analysis. I appreciate the fact that the authors point out how activity cliffs can also be used to examine multi-target activity relationships and links between sometimes-distant functional groups.

I agree with the authors' assessment that the activity cliff concept is underutilized in medicinal chemistry. Hopefully with the introduction of robust commercial software tools for the identification and exploitation of activity cliffs, the technique will be more widely used.

This review provides and excellent introduction to activity cliffs for those unfamiliar with the method. The paper is well referenced and will hopefully inspire a new group of users to continue to advance the method.
paper_title_zh: 推进活性悬崖概念
paper_abstract_zh: 活性悬崖概念在药物化学和化学信息学中引起了越来越多的关注。活性悬崖最初被定义为结构相似但针对同一靶标活性存在显著差异的化合物对。活性悬崖对于构效关系（SAR）分析和化合物优化具有重要意义，因为从悬崖中可以推断出小的化学修饰，这些修饰会导致活性发生大幅度的变化。除了基于单个化合物系列研究活性悬崖外，还可以通过挖掘化合物活性数据系统地识别它们。本文旨在提供一个简洁而详细的当前对活性悬崖理解的全貌。同时，也旨在向药物开发领域的普通读者介绍进一步细化的活性悬崖概念。
review_content_zh:
本文概述了结构-活性关系中活性悬崖的概念，并提供了一些在药物发现环境中应用该技术的实例。活性悬崖可以提供一种更好地理解化学结构与生物活性之间关系的方法，同时识别分子中对活性至关重要的区域。该综述面向非专家读者，应为不熟悉该主题的人提供足够的背景知识。熟悉活性悬崖的读者可能希望参考同一作者撰写的更专业的综述。这篇综述文笔流畅，易于理解，并为希望深入了解该主题的读者提供了许多关键参考文献。

作者将活性悬崖概念分解为各个组成部分，这对不熟悉该主题的读者将有所帮助。指出利用活性对数的差异可以使活性悬崖分数对化学家和生物学家更加直观，这可能是有益的。对化学信息学知识有限的读者将欣赏关于指纹相似性的讨论。然而，一幅图可能会使这些概念更加清晰。作者指出“计算的指纹Tc值通常难以从药物化学的角度解释”。根据我的经验，Tanimoto相似性通常是有意义的，这句话可能改为“计算的指纹Tc值*有时*难以解释”更为合适。作者提到匹配分子对（MMP）作为表达分子相似性的一种手段。

除了参考文献12和13外，还应包括我认为关于匹配分子对的奠基性论文。
Leach, A. G.; Jones, H. D.; Cosgrove, D. A.; Kenny, P. W.; Ruston, L.; MacFaul, P.; Wood, M.; Colclough, N.; Law, L. 匹配分子对作为优化药物性质的指南；水溶性、血浆蛋白结合和口服暴露的研究。J. Med. Chem. 2006, 49, 6672–6682.

随着化学家和生物学家追求更复杂的目标，有必要提高我们SAR分析的复杂性。我赞赏作者指出活性悬崖还可以用于研究多靶点活性关系以及有时相距较远的官能团之间的联系。

我同意作者的评估，即活性悬崖概念在药物化学中未被充分利用。希望随着用于识别和利用活性悬崖的强大商业软件工具的引入，该技术将得到更广泛的应用。

这篇综述为不熟悉该方法的读者提供了关于活性悬崖的出色介绍。该论文参考文献丰富，有望激励新一组用户继续推进该方法。

The paper is well referenced and will hopefully inspire a new group of users to continue to advance the method.
In addition to references 12 and 13, it would be useful to include what I consider to be the seminal paper on matched molecular pairs.
Those with a limited knowledge of chemoinformatics will appreciate the discussion of fingerprint similarity. However, a figure might make these concepts even more clear.

paper_title: Review of the nutritional composition, medicinal, phytochemical and pharmacological properties of Citrus reticulata Blanco (Rutaceae)
paper_abstract: Citrus reticulata Blanco is a moderately-sized fruit tree widely used as herbal medicine worldwide. The nutritional composition, medicinal uses, phytochemistry and pharmacological properties of C. reticulata were critically reviewed in the current study. The literature linked to C. reticulata properties was obtained from multiple internet sources including Elsevier, Google Scholar, SciFinder, Web of Science, Pubmed, BMC, Science Direct, and Scopus. Ethnopharmacological research identified antioxidants such as vitamin C, carotenoids and phenolic compounds, also a source of sugars, organic acids, amino acids, pectins, minerals and volatile organic compounds as components of C. reticulata . As a medicinal plant, C. reticulata is used for the treatment of dyspepsia, gastro-intestinal distension, cough with profuse phlegm, hiccup and vomiting. The crude extracts of C. reticulata fruits have depicted anti-inflammatory, anticholesterolemic, analgesic, antiasthmatic, antiscorbutic, antiseptic, antitussive, carminative, expectorant, stomachic. With more people becoming nutrition-conscious, there has been an increase in the demand for the use of citrus fruits and their by-products as traditional medicines for conventional healthcare in developing countries.
review_content:
The article is well written for the purpose intended. All the subject matter namely nutritional composition, medicinal, phytochemical and pharmacological properties as highlighted in the title of this article has been adequately reviewed and cited.

Secondary metabolites in plants are of major interest and are often taught in plant biochemistry courses. The content of secondary metabolites differ in different plant species and the use of such plant phytochemical for various purposes such as antibacterial, antimicrobial, anti cancer, anti-inflammatory etc, also differ among the plant species. This paper provides a comprehensive outlook and will be a good specimen to demonstrate the types of secondary metabolites present and its bioactive compounds in relation to pharmacological activities. The article can be a one stop reference on the properties of Citrus reticulata up to 2020.

Just a few minor typos are present, which are highlighted here.
paper_title_zh: 对Citrus reticulata Blanco（芸香科）的营养成分、药用、植物化学和药理特性的综述
paper_abstract_zh: 柑橘属植物Citrus reticulata Blanco是一种中等大小的果树，在全球范围内被广泛用作草药。本研究对C. reticulata的营养成分、药用用途、植物化学和药理特性进行了批判性综述。与C. reticulata特性相关的文献资料来源于多个互联网资源，包括Elsevier、Google Scholar、SciFinder、Web of Science、Pubmed、BMC、Science Direct和Scopus。民族药理学研究识别出C. reticulata含有抗氧化剂如维生素C、类胡萝卜素和酚类化合物，同时也是糖类、有机酸、氨基酸、果胶、矿物质和挥发性有机化合物的来源。作为一种药用植物，C. reticulata用于治疗消化不良、胃肠胀气、痰多咳嗽、呃逆和呕吐。C. reticulata果实的粗提物显示出抗炎、降胆固醇、镇痛、抗哮喘、抗坏血病、防腐、镇咳、驱风、祛痰和健胃等作用。随着越来越多的人关注营养健康，发展中国家对柑橘类水果及其副产品作为传统药物用于常规医疗保健的需求不断增加。
