paper_title: Incentives for pregnant mothers during antenatal care for better maternal and neonatal health outcomes in low and middle income countries: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
paper_abstract:
Background 
 Universal access to maternal, newborn, and child healthcare is essential for achieving Sustainable Development Goal 3, but the effectiveness of various incentive-based programs for pregnant mothers in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) remains uncertain. Objective of this systematic review was to determine if incentive-based interventions influenced maternal and neonatal health outcomes. 
 
 
 Methods 
 We conducted a search in various databases from inception. All incentive-based interventional studies conducted on pregnant women in LMICs were included. Evidence from the included trials was synthesized using risk ratios (RRs) to compare the outcomes between groups receiving incentives and not receiving incentives. The meta-analysis was conducted using random-effects model. We assessed the quality of the included studies using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool and reviewed the collected data to determine its suitability for meta-analysis. This study is registered in PROSPERO (CRD42021247681). 
 
 
 Results 
 Of the 3,897 records that were identified, 11 met eligibility criteria, all of which exhibited varying degrees of risk of bias, ranging from high to some concerns. Analysis of maternal outcomes across studies revealed no significant differences in the likelihood of delivering at a healthcare facility (RR 1.13, 95% CI: 0.86 to 1.47) and in frequency of prenatal care (RR 0.99, 95% CI: 0.88 to 1.12) between intervention and control groups. However, high levels of statistical heterogeneity were observed for both outcomes indicating variability among study results. Similarly, analysis of tetanus vaccine coverage showed no significant difference between groups (RR 1.00, 95% CI: 0.92 to 1.08), with moderate statistical heterogeneity observed. 
 
 
 Conclusion 
 The maternal and neonatal outcomes examined in this review did not have any significant differences in intervention group when compared to the control group. The interventions to address maternal health concerns need to follow a multifactorial approach. There is a need for extensive primary research studies in the future.
review_content:
Thank you for the opportunity to review this interesting paper. It reports the findings of a systematic review that searched for papers evaluating the impact on maternal and neonatal outcomes of offering incentives to pregnant women in low and middle income countries.
Overall this paper is very well written and interesting to read. My suggestions for edits are mainly for overall clarification not specific issues, to set the scene for the reader before you go into your well written sections. This is often the case when you know you subject well, but a few small clarifications and scene setting sentences would improve what is interesting and relevant research.


Minor
Introduction
Please could you move the detail of the SDG (MMR less than 70 per 100000 live deaths) to earlier on in the first paragraph in the Introduction? At the moment the reader has to wait till the sentence about Liberia to find out what the detail is.
I think this section would benefit too from a sentence or two on the overall issue with LMICs – you start off with describing South Africa and Asia in the second sentence. Could you add a bit to the first sentence along the lines of ‘…..countries and regions, particularly between higher and LMICs’ – or something similar.
I was also confused by the last sentence in the first paragraph: ‘The model also forecasts that 13 countries would achieve the target between 2030 to 2050; while the remaining 13 countries are likely to succeed after 2050’. In the previous sentence you stated that the study looks at data from 31 countries, the 2 comments about 13 countries would suggest that the study you cite looks at 26 countries. Please could you clarify why the 2 amounts in your last sentence don’t add up to 31?

In the Introduction you focus on maternal and neonatal mortality rates. It is not immediately obvious to me why you have chosen these outcomes to discuss. Please consider adding a short explanation of why you chose these specific outcomes, you might say that they are key outcomes that are linked to other important maternal/neonatal outcomes, or that they are proxy’s for other outcomes? For example in the second paragraph of the ‘Rationale: Why is this important?’ section in the Introduction in the first sentence you introduce some relevant outcomes such as pregnancy and childbirth-related complications, maybe introduce some of these in the first paragraph of the Introduction?

The ‘What is already known’ section could benefit from a short introduction paragraph. At the moment it starts with smoking cessation incentives, it would be good to set the scene with saying something along the lines of how incentives could benefit this area (in terms of reducing smoking and improving engagement with antenatal care for example) and improve maternal and child outcomes. This would help orientate the reader to what to expect in this section before it starts with more specific details. The last paragraph closes this section really nicely, starting with something similar as suggested would benefit it.

In the research questions section please could you write out in full what ‘IFA’ and ‘Inj TT’ refer to in 1b?

Methods

The Methods section is clear and very well written, it included everything I would expect to see in a systematic review. I was unable to see the search strategy in the repository – only PRISMA checklists and flowchart. Please could you check that the strategy is included – I just many not be able to see it - this is why I answered 'partly' to the question - Are sufficient details of the methods and analysis provided to allow replication by others?

In Outcomes – please could you clarify your definition of preterm delivery – i.e. born alive before 37 weeks, also for perinatal and neonatal deaths, and maternal deaths.
Discussion

Fourth paragraph in the Discussion section – the last 2 sentences are very similar – could this be a duplication?

Would it be possible to highlight that previously there were a small number of studies and with small sample sizes – and this study has not found a large number of studies – but most studies were RCTs – so assumably suitably powered? It would be good to have that additional information.

I really liked your last paragraph in the Discussion section about poverty not being the sole barrier for pregnant women to access healthcare services. Would it be possible to add another sentence or two to this paragraph if there is more evidence available similar to the violence you discussed in the second sentence?

In the ‘Implications for research’ section please could you consider moving the 4th and 5th paragraphs (evidence limited to LMIC and limited study resources for searching for non-English records) to the ‘Strengths and limitations of the study’ section – they read more like strengths and limitations rather than implications.

Typos/grammar
I only found a few typos/grammatical errors and mainly in the Results section:
In ‘Neonatal outcomes – 2. Perinat and neonatal deaths’ – ‘the data has not been adequate to conduct any analysis’ would read better as ‘the data was not adequate to conduct any analysis’
You also mix present and past tense in the Discussion:
Second paragraph – ‘there is no separate data on the same’ should read ‘there was no separate data on the same’, and ‘there is no adequate evidence to show the impact of incentives…’ should read ‘there was no adequate evidence to show the impact of incentives……’
paper_title_zh: 低收入和中等收入国家产前护理期间对孕妇的激励措施以改善母婴健康结果：系统综述与荟萃分析
paper_abstract_zh:
背景
普遍获得孕产妇、新生儿和儿童保健是实现可持续发展目标3的关键，但在低收入和中等收入国家（LMICs）中，针对孕妇的各种基于激励的计划的有效性仍不确定。本系统综述的目的是确定基于激励的干预措施是否影响了孕产妇和新生儿健康结果。

方法
我们从数据库建立之初进行了检索。纳入了在LMICs中针对孕妇进行的所有基于激励的干预研究。通过风险比（RRs）综合纳入试验的证据，比较接受激励和不接受激励组之间的结果。使用随机效应模型进行荟萃分析。我们使用Cochrane偏倚风险2.0工具评估了纳入研究的质量，并审查了收集的数据以确定其是否适合荟萃分析。本研究已在PROSPERO注册（CRD42021247681）。

结果
在识别的3,897条记录中，有11条符合纳入标准，所有研究均表现出不同程度的偏倚风险，从高风险到有一定关注。跨研究的孕产妇结果分析显示，在医疗机构分娩的可能性（RR 1.13，95% CI: 0.86至1.47）和产前护理频率（RR 0.99，95% CI: 0.88至1.12）方面，干预组和对照组之间无显著差异。然而，这两个结果均观察到高度统计学异质性，表明研究结果之间存在变异性。同样，破伤风疫苗覆盖率的分析显示两组之间无显著差异（RR 1.00，95% CI: 0.92至1.08），观察到中等程度的统计学异质性。

结论
本综述中考察的孕产妇和新生儿结果在干预组与对照组之间无显著差异。解决孕产妇健康问题的干预措施需要遵循多因素方法。未来需要大量原发性研究。
review_content_zh:
感谢有机会审阅这篇有趣的论文。该论文报告了一项系统综述的研究结果，该综述搜索了评估在低收入和中等收入国家向孕妇提供激励措施对母婴结局影响的论文。

总体而言，这篇论文写得非常好，读起来也很有趣。我的修改建议主要是为了整体上的澄清，而非具体问题，旨在为读者在你进入写得很好的部分之前设定背景。这通常在你对主题非常了解的情况下会发生，但一些小的澄清和背景设定句子会提升这项有趣且相关的研究。

次要问题
引言
你能否将可持续发展目标（每10万活产中孕产妇死亡率低于70）的细节提前到引言第一段的前面部分？目前读者需要等到关于利比里亚的句子才能了解具体细节。
我认为这一部分也可以从一两句话中受益，概述低收入和中等收入国家（LMICs）的整体问题——你在第二句开始描述南非和亚洲。你能否在第一句中添加一些内容，类似于“……国家和地区，特别是在高收入国家和低收入及中等收入国家之间”——或类似的内容。
我还对第一段的最后一句话感到困惑：“该模型还预测，到2030年至2050年间，将有13个国家实现目标；而其余13个国家可能在2050年后才能成功。”在前一句中，你提到该研究考察了31个国家的数据，这两处关于13个国家的评论似乎表明你引用的研究考察了26个国家。请澄清为什么你最后一句话中的两个数字加起来不等于31？

在引言中，你聚焦于母婴死亡率。我不太明白你为什么选择这些结局来讨论。请考虑添加一段简短的解释，说明你为什么选择这些特定结局，你可以说它们是与其他重要母婴结局相关的主要结局，或者它们是其他结局的代理指标？例如，在引言中“理由：为什么这很重要？”部分的第二段第一句中，你引入了一些相关结局，如与怀孕和分娩相关的并发症，也许可以在引言的第一段中引入一些这些内容？

“已知内容”部分可以从一段简短的引言中受益。目前它从戒烟激励措施开始，如果能先设定背景，说明激励措施如何在这一领域（例如减少吸烟和改善产前护理参与度）中带来益处并改善母婴结局，将有助于读者在开始更具体细节之前了解这一部分的内容。最后一段很好地结束了这一部分，以类似建议的内容开始会更有益。

在研究问题部分，请你在1b中完整写出“IFA”和“Inj TT”分别指什么？

方法

方法部分清晰且写得非常好，包含了我在系统综述中期望看到的所有内容。我无法在存储库中看到搜索策略——只有PRISMA清单和流程图。请检查是否已包含该策略——可能只是我看不到——这就是为什么我对“是否提供了足够的方法和分析细节以供他人复制？”这一问题回答“部分是”。

在结局部分——请澄清你对早产的定义——即出生时胎龄小于37周，以及围产期和新生儿死亡，以及孕产妇死亡。
讨论

讨论部分的第四段——最后两句话非常相似——这可能是一个重复？

是否可以强调以前研究的数量较少且样本量小——而这项研究并未发现大量研究——但大多数研究是随机对照试验（RCTs）——因此假设具有足够的效力？最好能有这些额外信息。

我非常喜欢你在讨论部分最后一段关于贫困并非孕妇获取医疗服务的唯一障碍的内容。如果还有更多类似你在第二句中讨论的暴力的证据，是否可以在这段中再添加一两句话？

在“对研究的启示”部分，请考虑将第四和第五段（证据仅限于LMIC和有限的资源用于搜索非英语记录）移至“研究的优势和局限性”部分——它们读起来更像是优势和局限性而非启示。

错别字/语法
我只发现了一些错别字/语法错误，主要在结果部分：
在“新生儿结局——2. 围产期和新生儿死亡”中——“the data has not been adequate to conduct any analysis”读起来不如“the data was not adequate to conduct any analysis”好。
你在讨论部分也混用了现在时和过去时：
第二段——“there is no separate data on the same”应读作“there was no separate data on the same”，而“there is no adequate evidence to show the impact of incentives…”应读作“there was no adequate evidence to show the impact of incentives……”。

reasons: Overall this paper is very well written and interesting to read.

I was also confused by the last sentence in the first paragraph: ‘The model also forecasts that 13 countries would achieve the target between 2030 to 2050; while the remaining 13 countries are likely to succeed after 2050’. In the previous sentence you stated that the study looks at data from 31 countries, the 2 comments about 13 countries would suggest that the study you cite looks at 26 countries. Please could you clarify why the 2 amounts in your last sentence don’t add up to 31?

only found a few typos/grammatical errors and mainly in the Results section: In ‘Neonatal outcomes – 2. Perinat and neonatal deaths’ – ‘the data has not been adequate to conduct any analysis’ would read better as ‘the data was not adequate to conduct any analysis’ You also mix present and past tense in the Discussion: Second paragraph – ‘there is no separate data on the same’ should read ‘there was no separate data on the same’, and ‘there is no adequate evidence to show the impact of incentives…’ should read ‘there was no adequate evidence to show the impact of incentives……’
Please could you move the detail of the SDG (MMR less than 70 per 100000 live deaths) to earlier on in the first paragraph in the Introduction?
I think this section would benefit too from a sentence or two on the overall issue with LMICs – you start off with describing South Africa and Asia in the second sentence.
The ‘What is already known’ section could benefit from a short introduction paragraph.

In the ‘Implications for research’ section please could you consider moving the 4th and 5th paragraphs (evidence limited to LMIC and limited study resources for searching for non-English records) to the ‘Strengths and limitations of the study’ section – they read more like strengths and limitations rather than implications.
Fourth paragraph in the Discussion section – the last 2 sentences are very similar – could this be a duplication?

paper_title: Individuality, phenotypic differentiation, dormancy and ‘persistence’ in culturable bacterial systems: commonalities shared by environmental, laboratory, and clinical microbiology
paper_abstract: For bacteria, replication mainly involves growth by binary fission. However, in a very great many natural environments there are examples of phenotypically dormant, non-growing cells that do not replicate immediately and that are phenotypically ‘nonculturable’ on media that normally admit their growth. They thereby evade detection by conventional culture-based methods. Such dormant cells may also be observed in laboratory cultures and in clinical microbiology. They are usually more tolerant to stresses such as antibiotics, and in clinical microbiology they are typically referred to as ‘persisters’. Bacterial cultures necessarily share a great deal of relatedness, and inclusive fitness theory implies that there are conceptual evolutionary advantages in trading a variation in growth rate against its mean, equivalent to hedging one’s bets. There is much evidence that bacteria exploit this strategy widely. We here bring together data that show the commonality of these phenomena across environmental, laboratory and clinical microbiology. Considerable evidence, using methods similar to those common in environmental microbiology, now suggests that many supposedly non-communicable, chronic and inflammatory diseases are exacerbated (if not indeed largely caused) by the presence of dormant or persistent bacteria (the ability of whose components to cause inflammation is well known). This dormancy (and resuscitation therefrom) often reflects the extent of the availability of free iron. Together, these phenomena can provide a ready explanation for the continuing inflammation common to such chronic diseases and its correlation with iron dysregulation. This implies that measures designed to assess and to inhibit or remove such organisms (or their access to iron) might be of much therapeutic benefit.
review_content:
Kell, Potgieter and Pretorius present a stimulating and argumentative review ranging from the interrelationships between the culturablilty of bacteria and their viability and any links these descriptions may have to defined physiological states, through a discussion of environmental bacteria and ultimately focusing on the human-associated microbiota, particularly those found in blood (without associated symptoms of sepsis) and their proposed roles in disease. Two central themes are developed beyond those that have been discussed extensively elsewhere: 1) the proposal that failure to culture bacteria from many samples often reflects dormancy and 2) that such dormant bacteria interact with host iron regulation to contribute to or directly cause a panoply of chronic diseases largely labelled as non-communicable.

At a general level I support the provocative stance taken by the authors. With 861 cited references, at the very least they provide a valuable resource for anyone wishing to consider the potential microbial contribution to diseases traditionally considered free of this aetiological component. Of course Helicobacter infection stands as a monument to the stupidity of dismissing this possibility in the face of carefully assembled evidence. Indeed this reviewer, who many years ago, was presented with a case of duodenal ulcer in his final medical exams, would probably have experienced quite a different career had he claimed a role for infection in causing his patient’s pathology.

In considering the specific points presented I have multiple concerns, the most significant of which I will indulge in outlining below.

Semantics present a central problem in considering bacterial viability and physiology and I broadly support the approach taken here. The authors do try to define their terms but some problems remain. In particular I take issue with the very broad application of term “Persisters” which should be reserved for cells that survive (have the potential to replicate) after exposure to an antimicrobial stress to which kills most cells in an actively growing culture of the organism concerned. Conflation of this term with “Dormancy” implies on the one hand that the persisting cells must have been dormant and on the other that dormancy and persistence represent the same physiological state in bacteria. This difficulty resurfaces later when they define dormancy but other problems emerge before then.

I was next concerned by the extensive use of the term “Differentiation”. I completely agree that what we used to think of as uniform bacterial populations are probably never so but the degree to which subpopulations may be considered differentiated rather than reflecting a range of adaptive responses or indeed, some degree of injury, is not considered here and again I think this leads to problems in considering their hypotheses under a unitary banner downstream. I consider differentiation to require phenotypic changes that are not directly reversible, as in the case of sporulation, whereas adaptation can involve expression of a single gene that can be reversed by its subsequent repression. I do agree that cell cycle contributes to the range of phenotypes in a pure bacterial culture and that this is not the only reason for their diversity (but was not enlightened by use of the term “modulo” in this regard).

The operational definition of dormancy given deliberately leaves open the possibility of metabolic activity and seems only to require that the cell so defined should not divide; this did not allow me to recognise which operational tests might be applied to enumerate or detect dormant cells. Subsequently the detection of molecular signals indicative of bacterial presence in samples from which they were not isolated in culture is taken as evidence of dormancy. In the first case do we accept any non-dividing cell as dormant and in the second I can (and will) offer multiple alternate explanations other than dormancy. Moreover, returning briefly to the conflation between dormancy and persisters, the recent work of John McKinney and colleagues shows that antibiotic exposed persisting cells are not necessarily non-dividing cells in the mycobacterial system he studied.

Alternative interpretations of the presence of bacterial 16SrDNA sequences in blood when culture fails to detect the organisms from which they derive, include the presence of dead, injured or moribund cells. If they are shown to be repeatedly present then they must either be able to persist in the face of clearance mechanisms or be supplied at a rate equal to their clearance; both seem equally plausible to the dormancy explanation to me. Moreover, why the first three explanations offered for “Not-yet-cultured” should apply to environmental bacteriology but not to clinical samples escapes me.

I am led to the conclusion that the authors have chosen to label evidence for discrepancies between culture and nucleic acid detection of bacteria in blood to give their hypotheses a simple headline. I have no problem with the proposal that human blood and tissues classically considered sterile in the absence of overt symptoms of infection are frequently exposed to bacteria and bacterial products that in many cases contribute to serious chronic disease. However, I consider the burden of available evidence currently provides many potential explanations within the field of microbiomics/metagenomics in contrast to the dormancy hypothesis offered here. Further, I feel this broad application of dormancy to bacterial phenotypes which, even in the case of Rpf dependency, have not been shown to result from a programme of gene expression that could be considered as differentiation, diminishes the value of the term. Indeed there remains no direct proof that dormancy of Mycobacterium tuberculosis underpins what we call latent tuberculosis infection and it is not essential to the observed clinical or pathological pattern, notwithstanding the widespread acceptance of this view by most researches, including me.

I am not fundamentally opposed to the ideas presented by Kell and colleagues but I do not think they are assisted by lack of attention to the contradictions I have identified above.

Finally I come to the iron dysregulation hypothesis and its pro-inflammatory consequences. It is beyond my expertise to comment on the plausibility of the inorganic chemistry deployed here or to review the evidence relating to more than a fraction of the conditions listed. The importance of the struggle between pathogens and host for access to iron is beyond question. When I entered the medical field of infectious disease it was fully recognised that depriving bacteria from iron was a potential therapeutic angle and indeed iron chelation was studied. Desferioxamine, a widely used agent in iron overload, was investigated and found to effectively deliver iron to the pathogen and the approach was set aside. More recently this agent has been identified as a major risk factor in serious fungal infection and guidance specifically recommends its avoidance. Newer agents seem not to suffer from this problem and the approach deserves renewed attention. However, I would not underestimate the ability of pathogens to outwit our pharmaceutical industry in the battle to sequester iron. While there are reasons beyond the host –pathogen tug-of war for iron to consider chelation as a therapeutic option, the potential for adverse effects is significant and I think the suggestion that omission of iron chelation from recent guidance on sepsis management is “shocking” is not justified.
Focussing briefly on the specific diseases cited and their relation to bacterial exposure in one form or another, I find that evidence cited frequently rests on what can be considered “fringe” hypotheses that have little currency in their respective fields. This is not to discourage their continued pursuit but it does weaken the strength of the authors’ argument when investigation of the supporting literature frequently leads to papers that are given little credence in the specialist field. Of course “cave Helicobacter” must remain on the table. But there, an accidental technical breakthrough led to an avalanche of convincing laboratory and clinical data.

In summary Kell, Potgieter and Pretorius have produced an interesting read which bring many important ideas to our attention. I am not convinced of the breadth of conditions to which they argue their ideas are applicable and I await with interest, demonstration of of how they may be practically pursued and some selected definitive proofs that iron-driven inflammatory disease is as important as they claim.
paper_title_zh: 个体性、表型分化、休眠及“持久性”在可培养细菌系统中的表现：环境、实验室及临床微生物学的共性
paper_abstract_zh: 对于细菌而言，复制主要通过二分裂生长实现。然而，在许多自然环境中，存在大量表型上休眠、不生长的细胞，这些细胞不会立即复制，并且在通常允许其生长的培养基上表现为“不可培养”。因此，它们通过常规的培养方法逃避检测。这种休眠细胞在实验室培养和临床微生物学中也可以观察到。它们通常对诸如抗生素等压力更具耐受性，在临床微生物学中通常被称为“持留菌”。细菌培养必然具有高度的亲缘关系，包容性适应度理论暗示，在生长速率的变化与其平均值之间进行权衡，具有概念上的进化优势，类似于对冲策略。大量证据表明，细菌广泛利用这一策略。本文汇集了数据，展示了这些现象在环境、实验室和临床微生物学中的普遍性。大量证据（使用类似于环境微生物学中常见的方法）现在表明，许多所谓的非传染性、慢性炎症性疾病是由休眠或持留细菌的存在加剧的（如果不是主要引起的话），这些细菌成分引发炎症的能力是众所周知的。这种休眠（及其复苏）通常反映了游离铁的可利用程度。综合来看，这些现象可以轻易解释这类慢性疾病中常见的持续炎症及其与铁调节失衡的相关性。这意味着设计用于评估、抑制或去除这些生物体（或其获取铁的能力）的措施可能具有显著的治疗益处。
review_content_zh:
Kell、Potgieter和Pretorius呈现了一篇激发思考和富有争议的综述，内容涵盖细菌可培养性与其生存能力之间的相互关系，以及这些描述与定义明确的生理状态之间可能存在的联系。通过讨论环境细菌，最终聚焦于与人类相关的微生物群，尤其是那些在血液中发现的（且无败血症相关症状）及其在疾病中的假定角色。文章发展了两个核心主题，这两个主题超出了其他地方广泛讨论的范围：1）未能从许多样本中培养出细菌通常反映了细菌的休眠状态；2）这种休眠细菌通过与宿主铁调节的相互作用，导致或直接促成一系列被广泛标记为非传染性的慢性疾病。

在总体层面上，我支持作者们所采取的挑衅性立场。凭借861篇引用文献，至少他们为任何希望考虑微生物对传统上认为无此病因成分疾病的潜在贡献的人提供了宝贵资源。当然，幽门螺杆菌感染成为在面对精心汇编的证据时，轻率否定这一可能性的愚蠢行为的纪念碑。事实上，本评审人多年前在最终医学考试中遇到一例十二指肠溃疡病例，如果他当时声称感染在其患者病理中起作用，他的职业生涯可能会大不相同。

在考虑所提出的具体观点时，我有多个担忧，其中最显著的将在下方详细阐述。

在考虑细菌生存能力和生理学时，语义呈现了一个核心问题，我大体上支持这里采取的方法。作者确实试图定义他们的术语，但一些问题仍然存在。特别是，我对“持留菌”（Persisters）这一术语的广泛应用持保留意见，该术语应保留用于在暴露于杀死大多数活跃生长培养物中细菌的抗菌压力后仍能存活（具有复制潜力）的细胞。将这一术语与“休眠”混淆，一方面暗示持留细胞必须是休眠的，另一方面暗示休眠和持留代表细菌中相同的生理状态。这一困难在后续他们定义休眠时再次浮现，但在此之前还出现了其他问题。

接下来，我对“分化”这一术语的广泛使用感到担忧。我完全同意，我们过去认为的统一细菌种群可能从未如此，但亚种群被认为分化的程度，而不是反映一系列适应性反应或某种程度的损伤，在这里并未考虑，我认为这导致在后续统一旗帜下考虑其假设时出现问题。我认为分化需要不可直接逆转的表型变化，如孢子形成的情况，而适应可以涉及单一基因的表达，该表达可以通过其后续的抑制而逆转。我确实同意细胞周期有助于纯细菌培养中的表型范围，而这并非其多样性的唯一原因（但并未因使用“模数”这一术语而有所启发）。

所给出的休眠的操作定义故意留出了代谢活动的可能性，似乎只要求如此定义的细胞不应分裂；这并未让我识别出哪些操作测试可能应用于计数或检测休眠细胞。随后，将检测到指示细菌存在的分子信号作为样本中未培养出细菌的证据。在第一种情况下，我们是否接受任何非分裂细胞为休眠细胞？在第二种情况下，我可以（并且会）提供除休眠之外的多重替代解释。此外，简要回顾休眠与持留菌的混淆，John McKinney及其同事的最新研究表明，在抗生素暴露下的持留细胞在所研究的分枝杆菌系统中并不一定是非分裂细胞。

当培养未能检测到衍生出16SrDNA序列的细菌时，对血液中细菌16SrDNA序列存在的替代解释包括死亡、受伤或垂死的细胞。如果它们被反复显示存在，那么它们要么能够面对清除机制而持续存在，要么以等于其清除速率的速率供应；在我看来，这两种情况都与休眠解释同样合理。此外，为什么“尚未培养”的前三个解释适用于环境细菌学而不适用于临床样本，我不得而知。

我得出的结论是，作者选择将培养与核酸检测细菌之间差异的证据标签化，以给他们的假设一个简单的标题。我并不反对人类血液和组织在无明显感染症状的情况下，经常暴露于细菌和细菌产品，并在许多情况下促成严重慢性疾病的观点。然而，我认为目前可用的证据负担在微生物组学/宏基因组学领域提供了许多潜在解释，与这里提出的休眠假设形成对比。此外，我觉得将休眠广泛应用于细菌表型，即使在Rpf依赖性情况下，也并未显示出由可被视为分化的基因表达程序所致，这削弱了该术语的价值。事实上，仍无直接证据表明结核分枝杆菌的休眠是我们所称的潜伏性结核感染的基石，且并非所观察到的临床或病理模式所必需，尽管包括我在内的多数研究者普遍接受这一观点。

我并非从根本上反对Kell及其同事提出的观点，但我不认为他们因未关注我上述指出的矛盾而得到帮助。

最后，我谈谈铁失调假设及其促炎后果。超出我的专业范围，无法评论此处部署的无机化学的合理性，或审查与所列条件中一小部分相关的证据。病原体与宿主之间争夺铁的重要性毋庸置疑。当我进入传染病医学领域时，完全认识到剥夺细菌铁是一个潜在的治疗角度，确实研究了铁螯合作用。去铁胺，一种在铁过载中广泛使用的药物，被研究并发现能有效将铁递送给病原体，该方法被搁置。最近，该药物被发现是严重真菌感染的主要风险因素，指南特别建议避免使用。较新的药物似乎没有这个问题，该方法值得重新关注。然而，我不会低估病原体在与制药业争夺铁的斗争中智胜我们的能力。尽管有超出宿主-病原体拉锯战的理由考虑螯合作为治疗选项，但潜在的不良影响是显著的，我认为最近关于败血症管理指南中省略铁螯合的建议是“令人震惊的”并不合理。

简要聚焦于所引用的特定疾病及其与某种形式的细菌暴露的关系，我发现所引用的证据经常依赖于可以被认为是“边缘”的假设，这些假设在其各自领域内鲜有流通。这并非要阻止其继续追求，但当调查支持性文献时，频繁引向在该专业领域内鲜有信誉的论文，这确实削弱了作者论点的力度。当然，“幽门螺杆菌之洞”必须保留在桌面上。但那里，一个偶然的技术突破引发了一系列令人信服的实验室和临床数据。

总之，Kell、Potgieter和Pretorius呈现了一篇引人入胜的读物，将许多重要观点带到我们面前。我并不确信他们主张其观点适用的条件范围，我满怀兴趣地期待他们如何实际追求这些观点，以及一些选择性确凿的证据，证明铁驱动的炎症性疾病如他们所声称的那么重要。

reasons: At a general level I support the provocative stance taken by the authors.
In considering the specific points presented I have multiple concerns, the most significant of which I will indulge in outlining below.
I am led to the conclusion that the authors have chosen to label evidence for discrepancies between culture and nucleic acid detection of bacteria in blood to give their hypotheses a simple headline.
However, I consider the burden of available evidence currently provides many potential explanations within the field of microbiomics/metagenomics in contrast to the dormancy hypothesis offered here.

Further, I feel this broad application of dormancy to bacterial phenotypes which, even in the case of Rpf dependency, have not been shown to result from a programme of gene expression that could be considered as differentiation, diminishes the value of the term.

Indeed there remains no direct proof that dormancy of Mycobacterium tuberculosis underpins what we call latent tuberculosis infection and it is not essential to the observed clinical or pathological pattern, notwithstanding the widespread acceptance of this view by most researches, including me.
In summary Kell, Potgieter and Pretorius have produced an interesting read which bring many important ideas to our attention.

I am not convinced of the breadth of conditions to which they argue their ideas are applicable and I await with interest, demonstration of of how they may be practically pursued and some selected definitive proofs that iron-driven inflammatory disease is as important as they claim.
Semantics present a central problem in considering bacterial viability and physiology and I broadly support the approach taken here.
The authors do try to define their terms but some problems remain.
I was next concerned by the extensive use of the term “Differentiation”.
This difficulty resurfaces later when they define dormancy but other problems emerge before then.
I am not fundamentally opposed to the ideas presented by Kell and colleagues but I do not think they are assisted by lack of attention to the contradictions I have identified above.
I am led to the conclusion that the authors have chosen to label evidence for discrepancies between culture and nucleic acid detection of bacteria in blood to give their hypotheses a simple headline.

paper_title: Cigarette consumption in adult dual users of cigarettes and e-cigarettes: a review of the evidence, including new results from the PATH study
review_content:
Summary: The authors conducted secondary analysis of cross-sectional and longitudinal PATH data to compare cigarette consumptions among dual users of cigarettes and e-cigarettes. The authors also present a review of published literature on this topic.
These reviewers has the following comments.
 1. The authors describe e-cigarettes as “reduced-risk tobacco products (RRP)”. While there is no doubt that e-cigs have considerably lower exposure to many of the HPHCs compared to combustible cigarettes and therefore present lower risks relative to cigarettes, the evidence is still emerging regarding these products. The authors should therefore consider identifying these products as “Potential Reduced-Risk Products” (PRRP).
 2. While we understand that recall bias may complicate inferences on tobacco product use history and the “correction” applied by the authors seems reasonable, the authors should consider including a results table for descriptive statistics (with and without correction) in the Supplement, to allow the reader judge for themselves regarding impact of this correction.
 3. The authors conclude that “smokers who become duals users will reduce their disease risk to some extent”. This is an extremely broad generalization, particularly given the authors own conclusion that the reduction in cigarettes is “fairly modest”. There is no empirical evidence to support this statement of risk reduction among the entire category of dual users, even to “some extent”. A recent report indicates that dual users are a very heterogenous group[ref-1],[ref-2]. Indeed, established every day frequent e-cigarette users may smoke far fewer cigarettes than current smokers thereby substantially reducing exposure to many of the HPHCs. This may lead to lowering of disease risks. In order to achieve the optimum outcome of reducing smoking related diseases, adult smokers must switch completely from cigarettes to e-cigs. We recommend that the authors either delete or modify the statement with appropriate caveats.
 4. There are several points for consideration to refine the methodology used in this manuscript:
     1. In the method section, the authors describe that the analysis is limited to every day cigarette smokers. The authors described “all the analyses were weighted, based on weighting factors for Wave 1”. In PATH user guide (Section 5), there are various types of weights. It is not clear whether the cross-sectional analysis (Q1) was conducted separately using cross-sectional weights of each wave to ensure the representativeness of the results. Longitudinal analysis should be conducted using longitudinal weights. In this case, wave 3 weights should be applied to answer research questions 2 and 3. The authors must clearly specify which weight was used for each analysis (Q1-Q3).
     2. The data is limited to ‘current everyday cigarette smokers at each Wave with data available on CC’. As reported by Borland et. al. (2019)[ref-3] and Smith et al. (2021)[ref-1] cigarette consumption differs significantly between every day and some day cigarette smokers and different segment of dual users. To obtain a complete picture of the current cigarette smoker population, the authors should consider including some day smokers in the analysis. This group more likely represents a larger proportion of dual users and provides a more comprehensive view of the cigarette consumption data for dual users. We note that indeed, there are cigarette consumption data in PATH for some day smokers.
     3. To answer Q3, the cigarette consumption was “compared in those who did or did not become dual users”. However, since Q3 is asking “is baseline consumption related to later initiation of e-cigarettes”. A logistic regression model with e-cigarette initiation as the outcome measure and cigarette consumption being the covariate would be more appropriate to answer Q3.
     4. Based on the current analysis description for Q3, the analysis will compare exclusive cigarette smokers who did or did not become dual users. A clearer description of ‘dual user’ needs to be given as it is shown in Table 3 there are three types of ‘Definition of Use’. Does the heading ‘Became users’ in the ‘Ever Established’ row mean exclusive daily smokers who became ever established users of e-cigarette? Please clarify.
     5. The authors should clearly describe if R survey package is used in the analysis. While the R-program is appropriate to conduct statistical analysis, R survey package allows the researcher to utilize the full-sample weight, variance estimation method, BRR-Fay replicate weights, and that Fay’s factor are correctly specified (See PATH User Guide, Appendix B for example R program code). The authors must specify whether replicate weights and Fay’s correction factor were used in current analyses.
     6. Authors state that “nine predictor variables [were] selected, using a forward stepwise approach, including variables significant at p<0.05”. It is not clear what variables were considered and the rationale for selection of the variables... The age range category “55+ years” for the variable ‘age range when first started smoking cigarettes every day’ should not be included as the data analysis is limited to 18 to 54 years.
     7. Authors only included respondents “aged 18 to 54 years at Wave 1 (as e-cigarette use proved to be very uncommon in those aged 55+ years”. A quick analysis revealed that by excluding individuals aged 55 or older, around 14% of the sample size is excluded among both current established and former established e-cigarette users at Wave 1. This phrase “(as e-cigarette use proved to be very uncommon in those aged 55+ years)” should be deleted since the data does not appear to support the statement.
 1. In the result section, the table captions should include more detail descriptions and definitions. For all result tables, the phrase ‘among every day smokers’ should be added if the analysis is only conducted among every day smokers. Does the table footnote ‘NS’ mean ‘not significant’? If yes, the corresponding footnote should be ‘p>0.05’ instead of ‘p<=0.05’. The ‘dual use’ term becomes very confusing when it is corresponding to three meanings (i.e., current establish e-cigarette use, ever established e-cigarette use and current every day e-cigarette use). The authors should be more precise.
     1. Table 1. Table caption should include ‘among every day smokers’ if the analysis is only conducted among every day smokers. There are three columns of ‘dual users’. The author needs to clarify the definitions of these three types of ‘dual users’.
     2. Table 2. The word ‘e-cigarette’ should be added to ‘current established use’, ‘ever established use’, and ‘current every day use’. The ‘No No’, ‘Yes Yes’, ‘No Yes’, ‘Yes No’ combinations should be clearly labeled with CS and ECIG to clearly identify the groups being considered.
     3. Table 3. The word “e-cigarette” should be specified in the ‘Definition of Use’ column. And the dual use needs to be clearly defined (see previous comments in the method section).
 2. Literature review results
     1. Results related to Q2
        In the literature review section, some of the findings were drawn from studies with adolescent data. Five out of 13 studies (Table 6) referenced in the results include adolescent data. The authors should be consistent with the literature search criteria and either exclude studies on youth as that was considered out of scope for the review, modify their search criteria or provide a rationale regarding inclusion of only select publications with adolescent data.
     2. Results related to Q3.
        Based on Andler et al. 2016, the authors state that ‘heavier smokers were more likely to start vaping’. However, this does not accurately represent the results from the publication. Andler et al. 2016, state that ”82 % of dual users reported that vaping had enabled them to reduce their cigarette consumption, with a mean reduction of 8.9 cigarettes per day. These individuals were initially heavy smokers, smoking 21 cigarettes per day on average (the mean overall among smokers was 11.3 in 2014.” Just because the participants in the study were heavy smokers that does not establish causality. Furthermore, Andler et al. 2016, included adolescents (age 15+) in their study. The authors should consider providing more context around the statement on heavy smokers.
paper_title_zh: 香烟和电子烟双重使用成年人群的香烟消费：证据综述，包括PATH研究的新结果
paper_abstract_zh:
背景：建模电子烟使用对疾病风险的影响需要了解电子烟的普及对吸烟者香烟消费的影响。通过美国PATH研究的第1-3波数据和其他证据，我们试图回答三个问题：（Q1）双重使用者与单一吸烟者的消费是否有差异？（Q2）开始使用电子烟是否会影响香烟消费？（Q3）基线消费是否与后期电子烟的起始使用相关？

方法：PATH中的消费数据经过校正以消除明显的记录错误，电子烟使用被分类为已确立或每日使用，并针对人口统计学特征、酒精、药物和其他烟草产品的使用以及开始吸烟的年龄进行了调整。搜索识别了自2008年以来发表的其他研究，Q1通过横断面研究回答，Q2和Q3也通过前瞻性研究回答。

结果：（Q1）在PATH中，当前每日使用电子烟的双重使用者消费比单一吸烟者低2-3支/天，而在已确立使用者中未见到差异。从31项已发表研究中，当前或曾经使用电子烟的双重使用者消费并未降低。（Q2）在PATH研究中，成为每日双重使用者的个体消费持续减少，而回归单一吸烟的个体消费增加。13项已发表研究一致显示成为双重使用者的个体消费减少。（Q3）三项研究一致显示随后开始使用电子烟的吸烟者消费更高，但PATH中未见到显著差异。

结论：评估因PATH中每日电子烟使用者较少以及各研究在量化电子烟使用和结果呈现上的变异性而复杂化。由于开始使用电子烟与减少消费相关，未发现双重使用者和单一吸烟者之间明显的横断面差异，这表明开始使用电子烟的吸烟者最初消费较高，但支持这一点的证据有限。鉴于电子烟相比香烟的疾病风险低得多，成为双重使用者的吸烟者应能一定程度上降低其疾病风险。
review_content_zh:
### 摘要

作者对横断面和纵向的PATH数据进行了二次分析，以比较同时使用香烟和电子烟的双重用户的香烟消费情况。作者还对该主题的已发表文献进行了综述。

审稿人提出以下意见：

1. 作者将电子烟描述为“降低风险烟草产品（RRP）”。毫无疑问，与可燃香烟相比，电子烟对许多有害和潜在有害成分（HPHCs）的暴露显著降低，因此相对于香烟而言风险较低，但关于这些产品的证据仍在不断涌现。因此，作者应考虑将这些产品标识为“潜在降低风险产品”（PRRP）。

2. 我们理解回忆偏倚可能会使烟草产品使用历史的推断复杂化，作者所应用的“修正”似乎合理，但作者应在补充材料中包括一个描述性统计结果的表格（有和没有修正），以便读者自行判断这一修正的影响。

3. 作者得出结论认为“成为双重用户的吸烟者将在一定程度上降低其疾病风险”。这是一个极其宽泛的概括，尤其是考虑到作者自己得出的结论是香烟减少的幅度“相当有限”。没有实证证据支持在整个双重用户类别中存在风险降低的情况，即使是“在一定程度上”。最近的一份报告指出，双重用户是一个非常异质化的群体[ref-1],[ref-2]。事实上，每天频繁使用电子烟的已建立用户可能比当前吸烟者吸食的香烟少得多，从而大幅减少对许多HPHCs的暴露。这可能导致疾病风险的降低。为了实现减少吸烟相关疾病的最优结果，成年吸烟者必须完全从香烟转向电子烟。我们建议作者要么删除该声明，要么在适当的警告下进行修改。

4. 有几个要点需要考虑以完善本文所使用的方法：
   1. 在方法部分，作者描述了分析仅限于每天吸烟的吸烟者。作者描述了“所有分析均根据第一波的权重因子进行了加权”。在PATH用户指南（第5节）中，有各种类型的权重。尚不清楚横断面分析（Q1）是否分别使用了每波的横断面权重以确保结果的代表性。纵向分析应使用纵向权重。在这种情况下，第三波的权重应应用于回答研究问题2和3。作者必须明确说明每个分析（Q1-Q3）使用了哪种权重。
   2. 数据仅限于“每个波次当前每天吸烟且在CC上有数据的吸烟者”。正如Borland等人（2019年）[ref-3]和Smith等人（2021年）[ref-1]所报告的，每天吸烟和某些天吸烟的吸烟者以及不同双重用户群体的香烟消费存在显著差异。为了全面了解当前吸烟者群体，作者应考虑将某些天吸烟者纳入分析。这一群体更有可能代表更大比例的双重用户，并提供更全面的关于双重用户香烟消费数据的视图。我们注意到，PATH中确实有某些天吸烟者的香烟消费数据。
   3. 为了回答Q3，香烟消费是在“成为或未成为双重用户的人”之间进行比较的。然而，由于Q3询问的是“基线消费是否与后期开始使用电子烟相关”。使用电子烟开始作为结果变量，香烟消费作为协变量的逻辑回归模型更适合回答Q3。
   4. 根据当前对Q3的分析描述，分析将比较成为或未成为双重用户的独家香烟吸烟者。需要更清楚地描述“双重用户”的定义，因为如表3所示，有三种“使用定义”。在“Ever Established”行中的“Became users”标题是否意味着成为电子烟的已建立用户的独家每天吸烟者？请澄清。
   5. 作者应明确描述是否在分析中使用了R调查包。虽然R程序适合进行统计分析，但R调查包允许研究人员利用全样本权重、方差估计方法、BRR-Fay复制权重，并确保Fay因子正确指定（参见PATH用户指南，附录B中的示例R程序代码）。作者必须说明当前分析中是否使用了复制权重和Fay修正因子。
   6. 作者指出“选择了九个预测变量，使用前向逐步方法，包括在p<0.05时显著的变量”。尚不清楚考虑了哪些变量以及选择这些变量的理由……对于变量“开始每天吸烟时的年龄范围”中的“55+岁”年龄范围类别不应包括在内，因为数据分析仅限于18至54岁。
   7. 作者仅包括“在第一波时年龄在18至54岁之间的受访者（因为电子烟使用在55岁及以上人群中非常罕见）”。快速分析显示，排除55岁或以上的人后，在第一波中当前已建立和以前已建立的电子烟用户中，约有14%的样本量被排除。由于数据似乎不支持该声明，因此应删除该短语“（因为电子烟使用在55岁及以上人群中非常罕见）”。

1. 在结果部分，表格标题应包括更详细的描述和定义。对于所有结果表格，如果分析仅限于每天吸烟者，应添加短语“在每天吸烟者中”。表格脚注“NS”是否意味着“不显著”？如果是，相应的脚注应为“p>0.05”而不是“p<=0.05”。“双重使用”一词在对应三种含义（即当前已建立电子烟使用、曾经已建立电子烟使用和当前每天电子烟使用）时变得非常混淆。作者应更精确。
   1. 表1。如果分析仅限于每天吸烟者，表格标题应包括“在每天吸烟者中”。有三列“双重用户”。作者需要澄清这三种“双重用户”的定义。
   2. 表2。应在“当前已建立使用”、“曾经已建立使用”和“当前每天使用”中添加“电子烟”一词。应明确标记“No No”、“Yes Yes”、“No Yes”、“Yes No”组合，并使用CS和ECIG清楚地识别所考虑的组。
   3. 表3。应在“使用定义”列中指定“电子烟”一词。并且需要明确定义双重使用（见方法部分之前的评论）。

2. 文献综述结果
   1. 与Q2相关的结果
      在文献综述部分，一些发现来自包含青少年数据的研究。在结果中引用的13项研究中有5项（表6）包括青少年数据。作者应保持文献检索标准的一致性，要么排除关于青少年的研究，因为这在综述中被认为超出范围，要么修改其检索标准，或提供关于仅包括含有青少年数据的选定出版物的理由。
   2. 与Q3相关的结果
      基于Andler等人2016年的研究，作者指出“重度吸烟者更有可能开始使用电子烟”。然而，这并不准确反映该出版物中的结果。Andler等人2016年指出，“82%的双重用户报告称，使用电子烟使他们能够减少香烟消费，平均每天减少8.9支香烟。这些个体最初是重度吸烟者，平均每天吸21支香烟（2014年吸烟者的平均值为11.3支）。”仅仅因为研究中的参与者是重度吸烟者，并不能确立因果关系。此外，Andler等人2016年的研究包括了青少年（15岁及以上）。作者应考虑在关于重度吸烟者的声明中提供更多背景信息。

Table 3. The word “e-cigarette” should be specified in the ‘Definition of Use’ column.
And the dual use needs to be clearly defined (see previous comments in the method section).
It is not clear whether the cross-sectional analysis (Q1) was conducted separately using cross-sectional weights of each wave to ensure the representativeness of the results.
Longitudinal analysis should be conducted using longitudinal weights.
In this case, wave 3 weights should be applied to answer research questions 2 and 3.
The authors must clearly specify which weight was used for each analysis (Q1-Q3).
To answer Q3, the cigarette consumption was “compared in those who did or did not become dual users”.
However, since Q3 is asking “is baseline consumption related to later initiation of e-cigarettes”.
A logistic regression model with e-cigarette initiation as the outcome measure and cigarette consumption being the covariate would be more appropriate to answer Q3.
A clearer description of ‘dual user’ needs to be given as it is shown in Table 3 there are three types of ‘Definition of Use’.
The authors should clearly describe if R survey package is used in the analysis.
The authors must specify whether replicate weights and Fay’s correction factor were used in current analyses.
It is not clear what variables were considered and the rationale for selection of the variables...

paper_title: Pathomechanisms Of Non-Coding RNAs, Hub Genes, and Lifestyle Related To The Oxidative Stress In Type 2 Diabetes And Cardiac Complications.
paper_abstract: Cytokine storms, oxidative stress, and hyperglycemia can enhance the risk of type 2 diabetes (T2D). Moreover, T2D may change the functional and structural heart. However, some signaling pathways, such as insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and hyperglycemia, can play in T2D, and various pathomechanics and pathophysiology involved in T2D are not understood. Moreover, it is well documented that the non-coding RNAs are potentially pivotal molecules in oxidative stress, inflammation, and cell death signaling pathways. Hence, long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) and microRNAs may have vital roles in oxidative stress, inflammation, metabolism, T2D, and cardiovascular systems. Non-coding RNAs can target hub gene networks and suppress or trigger various cascades. Furthermore, lifestyle is the other factor that may affect the prevalence of T2D. A sedentary lifestyle and excessive sitting can enhance inflammation, oxidative stress, and hyperglycemia. Here, we attempt to comprehend the role of hub genes, non-coding RNAs, and unhealthy lifestyles on the pathomechanics and pathophysiology of diabetic vascular complications.
review_content:
The manuscript (MS) by Hajibabaie et al. is a review on oxidative stress in diabetes with a focus on type 2 diabetes. While this MS is an extensive review, there are major issues that need to be addressed.
 1. The title of the MS is about non-coding RNAs and hub genes, but in the text, not much of non-coding RNAs was discussed. The title does not reflect the MS. Since the text focuses on type 2 diabetes, the title should reflect it.
 2. The writing is inconsistent. Few paragraphs are well written, but most paragraphs are difficult to read.
paper_title_zh: 非编码RNA、枢纽基因及生活方式与2型糖尿病及心脏并发症中氧化应激的病理机制
paper_abstract_zh: 细胞因子风暴、氧化应激和高血糖可以增加2型糖尿病（T2D）的风险。此外，T2D可能会改变心脏的功能和结构。然而，一些信号通路，如胰岛素抵抗、血脂异常和高血糖，在T2D中的作用，以及涉及T2D的各种病理机制和病理生理学尚未被充分理解。此外，已有大量文献表明，非编码RNA是氧化应激、炎症和细胞死亡信号通路中潜在的关键分子。因此，长链非编码RNA（lncRNAs）和微RNA可能在氧化应激、炎症、代谢、T2D和心血管系统中发挥重要作用。非编码RNA可以靶向中心基因网络，抑制或触发各种级联反应。此外，生活方式是另一个可能影响T2D患病率的因素。久坐不动的生活方式和过度久坐可以增强炎症、氧化应激和高血糖。在此，我们试图理解中心基因、非编码RNA和不健康生活方式对糖尿病血管并发症的病理机制和病理生理学的影响。
review_content_zh:
Hajibabaie等人的手稿（MS）是一篇关于糖尿病中氧化应激的综述，重点关注2型糖尿病。尽管这篇MS进行了广泛的综述，但仍存在一些需要解决的主要问题。
1. MS的标题涉及非编码RNA和枢纽基因，但在文本中，对非编码RNA的讨论并不多。标题未能反映MS的内容。由于文本聚焦于2型糖尿病，标题应体现这一点。
2. 写作风格不一致。少数段落写得很好，但大多数段落难以阅读。

paper_title: Dynamics of Zika virus outbreaks: an overview of a mathematical modeling approach
paper_abstract: Background. The Zika virus was first discovered in 1947. It was neglected until a major outbreak occurred on Yap Island, Micronesia, in 2007. Teratogenic effects resulting in microcephaly in newborn infants is the greatest public health threat. In 2016, the Zika virus epidemic was declared as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Consequently, mathematical models were constructed to explicitly elucidate related transmission dynamics.
review_content: Reviewer 2 (John Palmer) Basic reporting This literature review article provides a nice introduction to mathematical modeling in the context of Zika. The body of literature that it gathers and synthesizes provides a very useful starting point for anyone wishing to enter this area of research. That said, I think it needs to be improved significantly before it is ready to be published. 1. Much of the writing is difficult to follow and should be revised and closely edited. ### Response ### We have revised the manuscript. The manuscript has been edited by Elsevier Language Editing Services. 2. The literature is properly referenced in the text, but some important sources appear to be missing (for example Adams and Kapan. 2009. “Man Bites Mosquito: Understanding the Contribution of Human Movement to Vector-Borne Disease Dynamics.” Edited by Alison P. Galvani. PLoS ONE 4 (8).) ### Response ### We have included the recommended paper. The following sentences have been added on Page 14: “Another example is the contributions of the human mobility patterns and the subpopulation of mosquitoes to the epidemiology of vector-borne diseases (Adams & Kapan, 2009). The model suggested that the places people visit frequently but for a short amount of time are at risk for the spread of diseases. However, the distribution patterns of the mosquitoes and human movement characteristics are also important.” In addition, we have also added some other papers. 3. The structure is fine, although I recommend making it clearer in the beginning of the Abstract that this is a review article. ### Response ### Revised as suggested. We have re-titled the manuscript to “Dynamics of Zika Virus Outbreaks: An Overview of a Mathematical Modeling Approach”. We have also added “In this review article…” in the abstract. 4. I am also not sure the authors need to go into such detail about how they selected the articles -- or that they need to limit the literature to that found in this type of methodical survey. ### Response ### We were asked from the journal to declare our search criteria before proceeding to the revision step. So, we have to put this clarification. Experimental design This is not primary research but rather a literature review, summarizing and synthesizing existing work in this area. It appears to fall within the aims and scope of PeerJ. The research question is broad (essentially the article asks what has been done with respect to mathematical modeling relevant to Zika dynamics). It is not entirely clear that it fills a real knowledge gap, although it is surely helpful to have this body of literature synthesized. The methods in this case are the search criteria. They are clearly described, but I am not convinced that this type of formal survey is needed. I would opt for looser search criteria in order to ensure that all relevant literature has been located. For instance, there are probably important sources that do not contain the term "mathematical model" (even if that is what they provide). ### Response ### We were asked from the journal to declare our search criteria before proceeding to the revision step. So, we have to put this clarification. Indeed, we used some other few search teams but the results were not much different. We have added two other search terms; “dynamics” and “modeling”. A sentence on Page 6 now reads “In the first step, we used the search terms “dynamics,” “mathematical model,” “modeling,” and “vector-borne” together with the names of vector-borne diseases such as chikungunya, dengue, malaria, West Nile, and Zika.” We tried our best to cover all aspects. However, some important papers may be still missed. We tried to add some according to the reviewer’s suggestion. Validity of the findings The main conclusion is the summary of existing models. From this, the authors note that there has been a lack of application of these models in the field by health professionals, and they suggest some ways in which that might be changed. This is an interesting discussion, but the authors might expand on different ways in which this field implementation could occur, as well as different uses of simple versus complex models. ### Response ### Revised as suggested. We have added the following sentences to the last paragraph of the perspective section (Page 24): “To fully implement mathematical modeling, one must persuade policy makers to include the methods and try to prove that they are necessary. In this case, the translation of mathematical language into political contexts is crucial. Moreover, simple and complex models should be exploited differently. Simple models can be produced in a timely fashion to provide an estimation of the possible impacts. In contrast, complex models require more time to develop but are far more realistic. The models are much more powerful in terms of predictive capability. The preparation of complicated models before outbreaks is recommended.”
paper_title_zh: 寨卡病毒爆发的动力学：数学建模方法概览
paper_abstract_zh: 背景。寨卡病毒最早发现于1947年。直到2007年在密克罗尼西亚的雅浦岛上发生大规模爆发，该病毒才受到关注。其导致的胎儿小头畸形等致畸效应是最大的公共卫生威胁。2016年，寨卡病毒疫情被宣布为国际关注的公共卫生紧急事件（PHEIC）。随后，构建了数学模型以明确阐释相关的传播动力学。
review_content_zh:
### 审稿人2（John Palmer）的基本评价

这篇文献综述文章在寨卡病毒背景下对数学建模提供了良好的入门介绍。它所汇集和综合的文献为任何希望进入该研究领域的人提供了非常有用的起点。尽管如此，我认为在发表之前还需要进行显著的改进。

1. 许多写作内容难以理解，应进行修订和仔细编辑。### 回应 ### 我们已修订了手稿。手稿已由Elsevier语言编辑服务进行了编辑。

2. 文献在文本中得到了适当的引用，但似乎缺少了一些重要来源（例如Adams和Kapan. 2009. “Man Bites Mosquito: Understanding the Contribution of Human Movement to Vector-Borne Disease Dynamics.” 由Alison P. Galvani编辑。PLoS ONE 4 (8)）。### 回应 ### 我们已包括推荐的论文。在第14页添加了以下句子：“另一个例子是人类移动模式和蚊子亚群对虫媒传染病流行病学的影响（Adams & Kapan, 2009）。该模型表明，人们频繁但短暂访问的地方有疾病传播的风险。然而，蚊子的分布模式和人类移动特征也很重要。”此外，我们还添加了一些其他论文。

3. 结构尚可，尽管我建议在摘要开头更清楚地说明这是一篇综述文章。### 回应 ### 按建议进行了修订。我们将手稿重新命名为“寨卡病毒爆发的动态：数学建模方法概览”。我们还在摘要中添加了“在这篇综述文章中……”。

4. 我也不确定作者是否需要如此详细地描述他们选择文章的过程——或者他们是否需要将文献限制在这种系统调查中找到的范围内。### 回应 ### 杂志要求我们在进行修订步骤之前声明我们的搜索标准。因此，我们必须提供这一澄清。

### 实验设计

这不是一项原始研究，而是一篇文献综述，总结和综合了该领域的现有工作。它似乎符合PeerJ的目标和范围。研究问题较为广泛（本质上文章询问了在寨卡动态相关的数学建模方面已经做了哪些工作）。尚不清楚它是否填补了真正的知识空白，尽管将这批文献综合起来无疑是有帮助的。在这种情况下，方法就是搜索标准。它们描述得很清楚，但我不确定是否需要这种正式的调查。我会选择更宽松的搜索标准，以确保找到所有相关文献。例如，可能有一些重要来源不包含“数学模型”这一术语（即使它们提供了相关内容）。### 回应 ### 杂志要求我们在进行修订步骤之前声明我们的搜索标准。因此，我们必须提供这一澄清。事实上，我们使用了一些其他搜索术语，但结果差异不大。我们在第6页添加了两个其他搜索术语；“动态”和“建模”。现在该页的一句话读作：“在第一步中，我们使用了‘动态’、‘数学模型’、‘建模’和‘虫媒’等搜索术语，以及如基孔肯雅热、登革热、疟疾、西尼罗河和寨卡等虫媒疾病的名称。”我们尽力涵盖所有方面。然而，可能仍有一些重要论文被遗漏。我们根据审稿人的建议尝试添加了一些。

### 研究结果的可靠性

主要结论是对现有模型的总结。由此，作者指出这些模型在实地应用中存在不足，并建议了一些可能改进的方法。这是一个有趣的讨论，但作者可以进一步探讨实地实施的不同方式，以及简单模型与复杂模型的不同用途。### 回应 ### 按建议进行了修订。我们在展望部分最后一段（第24页）添加了以下句子：“要完全实施数学建模，必须说服政策制定者纳入这些方法，并证明其必要性。在这种情况下，将数学语言转化为政治背景至关重要。此外，简单和复杂模型应有所不同地利用。简单模型可以及时制作，以提供可能影响的估计。相比之下，复杂模型需要更多时间开发，但更为现实。这些模型在预测能力方面要强大得多。建议在疫情爆发前准备复杂的模型。”

reasons: The body of literature that it gathers and synthesizes provides a very useful starting point for anyone wishing to enter this area of research.

The literature is properly referenced in the text, but some important sources appear to be missing (for example Adams and Kapan. 2009. “Man Bites Mosquito: Understanding the Contribution of Human Movement to Vector-Borne Disease Dynamics.” Edited by Alison P. Galvani. PLoS ONE 4 (8).)
I would opt for looser search criteria in order to ensure that all relevant literature has been located.
It is not entirely clear that it fills a real knowledge gap, although it is surely helpful to have this body of literature synthesized.
The main conclusion is the summary of existing models.
This is an interesting discussion, but the authors might expand on different ways in which this field implementation could occur, as well as different uses of simple versus complex models.
The structure is fine, although I recommend making it clearer in the beginning of the Abstract that this is a review article.

paper_title: Exploring antecedents of built environment for walkability of older adults: A systematic literature review
paper_abstract:
Background 
 This systematic literature review (SLR) explores how urban design influences walking access in the built environment for walking of older adults, summarizing existing studies. Examining various theories, it analyses themes like safety, security, comfort, convenience, aesthetics, governance, and policy frameworks. By critically reviewing the literature, it seeks to understand current research trends and suggest future directions. 
 
 
 Methods 
 The study employs an evidence-based systematic approach, following the standard procedure of SLR to identify relevant studies and extract information. 
 
 
 Results 
 It was found that five prominent theories dominated research literature: Active Aging Framework (AAF) (35.4%), Social-Ecological Model of Health Promotion (SEMHP) (25%), Community-Engaged Urban Design Theory (CEUDT) (18%), Neighbourhood Social Environment Theory (NSET) (11%), and the fifth Ecological Model of Aging (EMA) (8%). 
 Empirical research dominated (37.5%), followed by grounded theory (20.8%), case study (18.8%), comparative study (12.5%), document analysis (8.3%), and analytical research (2.1%) in terms of the research type. The SLR revealed that most research uses empirical methods and focuses on applying existing theories. 
 
 
 Conclusions 
 It identifies opportunities for future research, suggesting areas for model integration, advancement, and application. Notably, it highlights the potential of combining the two most relevant theories for interventions promoting older adults’ health through walkable environments. This review can aid practitioners and researchers in identifying the theoretical underpinning of key factors for designing walkable cities that cater to older adults’ needs. A potential limitation is its focus on dominant theories, excluding others that might offer valuable insights.
review_content:
This systematic literature review examines theoretical approaches to supportive environments for walking for older adults.

The authors’ approach to a systematic literature review is well documented, but confusing in some aspects. For example, the authors claim in the abstract to review themes such as safety, security, comfort, and convenience, but these terms and concepts are almost entirely absent from the paper.

The authors’ literature review framework is reasonable, in that they review papers with respect to the conceptual model employed, the research focus, and the research type, and they summarize the reviewed papers according to these dimensions. Yet many aspects of the review as written remain unclear or inadequately analyzed.

This critique will start with big-picture issues and then delve into some more nuanced potential refinements.
First, the framework of “BEW” or “Built Environment for Walking” seems to be inconsistent with what the authors find and discuss. The authors mention the importance of social environments and policy dynamics, so from the start the frame should be drawn much larger than the built environment. Perhaps built and social environments? The other term the authors use is “antecedents” which might be a good term, but if so the authors should use it more consistently and define it clearly. The term “antecedents” does not occur in any of the stated research questions.
The authors’ abstract suggests a comprehensive literature review of how urban design influences walking access and behavior for older adults. However, the authors have heavily focused on theoretical frameworks in their literature search, possibly filtering out empirical papers that are light on theory. I believe the authors’ contribution is still valuable, but the abstract should more accurately indicate the scope of the literature review conducted.

Systematic literature reviews generally include an evaluation of research quality. However, conventional evaluation criteria for research quality typically concern on quantitative analysis methods, such as research design, the presence of confounders, the use of blinding, the validation of data collection methods, and so forth (Ravensbergen and El-Geneidy, 2023) [Ref-1]. The authors are quite vague on their methods of evaluation for research quality. I would suggest that with the authors’ topical focus being on theoretical approaches and contributions, evaluation of research quality may not be relevant.

The authors mention that both “contribution type” and “research focus” are of interest. However, there is no description of different categories of contribution type. Are “contribution type” and “research focus” the same? At the bottom of page 8 the heading is “Contribution type” with no discussion of what this means. Then the following section is on “Research Focus” and identifies four types: 1) Model Development, 2) Model Testing, 3) Model Advancing, and 4) Model Integration. So it seems that a discussion of “Contribution Type” is missing or is perhaps synonymous with with “Research Focus.”

I found the section on the four different “Research Focuses” to be problematic. The four focuses, as I understand them, are Model Development, Model Testing, Model Advancement, and Model Integration.” After reading this section, I am still unclear on the differences. This section reads more like a miniature literature review rather than a conceptual section that defines what makes each of these foci different from each other. I am expecting to read brief definitions with perhaps one example. The goal should be for the reader to be able to tell when a paper falls in one category versus the other. After reading this section, I had no idea how a paper would be categorized into one of these foci.

In the results section on pages 11-12, the authors describe the different theories and characterize the publications falling under each theory type. What struck me is how similar the descriptions of the differing theories sounded. Several of them were described as “holistic” and several mentioned the effects of social, environmental, and individual factors on walking behaviors. Could the authors develop a framework that allows the reader to see the differences between these theoretical frameworks? Which frameworks cover topics or issues that are not covered by the others?

The lengthy paragraph on how far back the literature review should go back was not informative and lacked an empirical basis. For example, the claim “The SEMHP has had an ideal period of impact during the last 15-20 years” is not substantiated by data or a citation. The authors could establish a conventional time frame for their search (i.e. 20 years or 30 years) without including this paragraph. Or they could provide more evidence to support the claims in this paragraph.

The description of search terms that occurs in the second paragraph of page 5 does not correspond with the search terms actually employed in Table 1. The paragraph mentions the terms “safety,” “comfort” and “convenience” but none of these terms occur in Table 1. Meanwhile, Table 1 includes many search terms, such as “Walkability,” “Older Adults” and “Physical Activity” that are not described in the narrative. The authors should re-write this section to correspond to the searches that were actually conducted, and the narrative and the table should correspond closely to each other.

Several of the exclusion criteria do not seem to be necessary for exclusion. “Approached challenges and issues related to BEW development.” “Qualitatively discussed BEW concerning historical and current scenarios across various contexts, including sectoral, regional, national, international, etc.” Why would these be exclusion criteria? This is not obvious.
With regard to Research Types, I am not clear on how Empirical Research is different from Analytical Research. Both seem to be empirical and statistical in nature.

The discussion section is repetitive. The authors mention several times the potential benefits of interdisciplinary collaboration and the need for more model advancement and model integration. This section can be condensed.
paper_title_zh: 探索老年人步行环境前置因素的系统性文献综述
paper_abstract_zh:
背景
本系统文献综述（SLR）探讨了城市设计如何影响老年人步行可达性，总结了现有研究。通过审视多种理论，分析了安全、保障、舒适、便利、美学、治理和政策框架等主题。通过批判性地回顾文献，旨在理解当前研究趋势并提出未来方向。

方法
研究采用基于证据的系统方法，遵循SLR的标准程序来识别相关研究和提取信息。

结果
研究发现，五种主要理论主导了研究文献：积极老龄化框架（AAF）（35.4%）、健康促进的社会生态模型（SEMHP）（25%）、社区参与城市设计理论（CEUDT）（18%）、邻里社会环境理论（NSET）（11%）和第五种生态老龄化模型（EMA）（8%）。
在研究类型方面，实证研究占主导地位（37.5%），其次是扎根理论（20.8%）、案例研究（18.8%）、比较研究（12.5%）、文献分析（8.3%）和分析性研究（2.1%）。SLR显示，大多数研究使用实证方法，并侧重于应用现有理论。

结论
研究识别了未来研究的机遇，建议在模型整合、发展和应用方面进行探索。特别强调结合两种最相关理论以通过可步行环境促进老年人健康的干预潜力。本综述可以帮助实践者和研究人员识别设计满足老年人需求的可步行城市的关键因素的理论基础。一个潜在局限是其聚焦于主导理论，排除了可能提供有价值见解的其他理论。
review_content_zh:
本系统文献综述探讨了为老年人提供步行支持环境理论方法。

作者对系统文献综述的方法记录详尽，但在某些方面存在混淆。例如，作者在摘要中声称要审查安全、保障、舒适和便利等主题，但这些术语和概念在论文中几乎完全缺失。

作者的文献综述框架合理，他们根据所采用的概念模型、研究重点和研究类型来审查论文，并按照这些维度总结所审查的论文。然而，所写综述的许多方面仍然不清晰或分析不足。

本批评将从宏观问题开始，然后深入探讨一些更细微的潜在改进。
首先，“BEW”或“步行建筑环境”的框架似乎与作者发现和讨论的内容不一致。作者提到了社会环境和政策动态的重要性，因此从一开始，框架就应比建筑环境更为广泛。或许是建筑和社会环境？作者使用的另一个术语是“前因”，这可能是一个好术语，但如果是这样，作者应更一致地使用它并明确其定义。“前因”这一术语在所列的研究问题中并未出现。

作者的摘要表明，这是一项关于城市设计如何影响老年人步行访问和行为的全面文献综述。然而，作者在文献检索中过于关注理论框架，可能过滤掉了理论较少的实证论文。我认为作者的贡献仍然有价值，但摘要应更准确地指出所进行文献综述的范围。

系统文献综述通常包括对研究质量的评估。然而，研究质量的传统评估标准通常关注定量分析方法，如研究设计、混杂因素的存在、盲法的使用、数据收集方法的验证等（Ravensbergen和El-Geneidy，2023）[Ref-1]。作者对其研究质量评估方法相当模糊。我建议，鉴于作者的主题聚焦于理论方法和贡献，研究质量的评估可能不相关。

作者提到“贡献类型”和“研究重点”都值得关注。然而，没有描述不同类别的贡献类型。“贡献类型”和“研究重点”是相同的吗？在第8页底部，标题为“贡献类型”，但没有讨论其含义。接下来的部分是关于“研究重点”，并确定了四种类型：1）模型开发，2）模型测试，3）模型推进，4）模型整合。因此，似乎缺少了对“贡献类型”的讨论，或者可能与“研究重点”同义。

我发现关于四种不同“研究重点”的部分存在问题。据我理解，这四种重点是模型开发、模型测试、模型推进和模型整合。读完这一部分后，我仍不清楚它们之间的区别。这一部分更像是一个小型文献综述，而不是定义每种重点之间差异的概念性部分。我期望读到简短的定义，或许附上一个例子。目标应是使读者能够区分一篇论文属于哪一类别。读完这一部分后，我完全不知道如何将一篇论文归类到这些重点之一。

在第11-12页的结果部分，作者描述了不同的理论并概括了属于每种理论类型的出版物。令我惊讶的是，不同理论的描述听起来如此相似。其中几个被描述为“整体性”，并提到了社会、环境和个体因素对步行行为的影响。作者能否开发一个框架，使读者能够看到这些理论框架之间的差异？哪些框架涵盖了其他框架未涉及的主题或问题？

关于文献综述应追溯多久的冗长段落并未提供信息，且缺乏实证基础。例如，“SEMHP在过去15-20年期间具有理想的影响期”这一说法没有数据或引文支持。作者可以为其搜索确立一个常规时间框架（即20年或30年），而不包括这一段落。或者他们可以提供更多证据来支持这一段落的说法。

第5页第二段对搜索术语的描述与表1中实际使用的搜索术语不符。该段落提到了“安全”、“舒适”和“便利”等术语，但这些术语在表1中并未出现。同时，表1包括许多搜索术语，如“可步行性”、“老年人”和“体力活动”，这些在叙述中并未描述。作者应重写这一部分，以符合实际进行的搜索，叙述和表格应紧密对应。

有几个排除标准似乎没有必要。例如，“涉及BEW发展挑战和问题”的论文，“定性地讨论了BEW在各个背景下（包括部门、区域、国家、国际等）的历史和当前情景”。为什么这些会成为排除标准？这并不明显。
关于研究类型，我不清楚实证研究与分析研究的区别。两者似乎都具有实证和统计性质。

讨论部分重复性较高。作者多次提到跨学科合作的潜在益处以及更多模型推进和模型整合的必要性。这一部分可以压缩。
